#1688. Alex Scott: Chelsea, Man City receive fresh transfer update from Bournemouth owner

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 12:32, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 12:34

Bournemouth owner Bill Foley has delivered a fresh update on the future of in-demand midfielder Alex Scott ahead of the January transfer window.

The 23-year-old has established himself as one of the brightest midfield talents in the Premier League since joining the Cherries from Bristol City for around £25m in August 2023.

Scott has made a total of 95 appearances for Bournemouth across all competitions and was a key cog in the Cherries side that finished sixth in the Premier League last season, securing Europa League qualification.

The Guernsey-born star received his first two senior England caps during the September/October international break, but he has since been sidelined with a hamstring injury, missing Bournemouth’s last seven games.

At a time when Scott is focused on his recovery, speculation over his long-term future at the Vitality Stadium continues to grow ahead of the winter window.

The Evening Standard claims that Chelsea saw a £64m bid for Scott rejected by Marco Rose's Bournemouth in the summer, while approaches from other English clubs were knocked back.

Xabi Alonso’s side – who failed to replace Enzo Fernandez in the summer – are said to maintain a firm interest in Scott, while Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United have also been linked with the midfielder.

Scott is under contract at the Vitality Stadium until June 2028 and he is understood to have turned down the club’s opening offers of an extension, promoting speculation over a January exit.

The Cherries are reportedly open to selling Scott midway through the season should an offer worth around £100m arrive.

While Bournemouth chief Foley has acknowledged that the lure of joining a bigger club is there for Scott, he has insisted that the Cherries “haven’t given up” trying to convince him to sign a new deal.

Foley is also hopeful that Bournemouth offering their key players six-figure wages will become “commonplace”.

Speaking on talkSPORT about Scott’s future, Foley said: “At this point, we're convinced we're the right place for Alex to be and to stay, and we'll keep on addressing the contract issues with Alex as we move through this year.

“We'd love to have Alex stay here and sign a new contract and be part of this team for the long haul.

“We haven't given up, but sometimes players get stars in their eyes, and they think that Chelsea or Manchester City is the right place to go.

“We believe, if we keep on buying infrastructure and a common thread of leadership across the team then we will start keeping more and more players.

“People will be surprised about that, and they'll be able to earn substantial wages here.”

The 81-year-old added: “We have to respect the fact that a lot of our players are younger, and they've come to Bournemouth with the expectation that they'll get time to play and perhaps move on to a bigger team.

“We recognise that my job is to make players feel comfortable and provide them with the infrastructure they need to understand that.”

Bournemouth, meanwhile, are said to have identified two potential replacements for Scott should he ultimately decide to seek pastures new.

#1685. Arsenal's appeal against Max Dowman's red card is REJECTED: Gunners star, 16, to serve ban after sending off in Fleetwood defeat - which left Mikel Arteta fuming - as club legend sends warning

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER and ISAAN KHAN, REPORTER

Published: 13:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 14:42 EDT, 29 October 2026

The FA have upheld Max Dowman’s three-match ban after the teenager was sent off in Arsenal’s shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

Arsenal appealed the red card after Dowman was sent off in the 86th minute of Tuesday’s defeat for kicking out in retaliation to a scissor challenge by Harrison Neal, who was shown a yellow card.

But the 16-year-old will now miss Arsenal’s Premier League matches against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle after the FA stuck with the on-field decision one day after the Premier League champions lodged their appeal.

As the teenager left the field, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta gave him a scathing look and uttered a few words to the young attacker, understood to be: ‘Get to the changing room, Max’.

Dowman has turned out four times this season and his suspension comes as a blow after injuries to Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke.

His dismissal split opinion with Arsenal legend Paul Merson among those who jumped to his defence on the Sky Sports broadcast on Tuesday evening.

Arsenal have failed in their appeal to have Max Dowman's three-match ban overturned

Dowman was dismissed for his reaction to a strong challenge from Fleetwood's Harrison Neal

Fellow Arsenal legend Ray Parlour however, has urged Dowman to learn from his mistakes following his midweek dismissal.

It was Dowman's second red card this month, having also been sent off while representing England's Under 19s.

And Parlour - part of the Invincibles side which went unbeaten in winning the Premier League in 2004 - said: ‘Well, I thought he (Dowman) was a little bit unlucky, if I'm being honest. He was tangled with the legs, but he's a young man, he's going to make mistakes.

‘He's got to learn from it, that's all. I'm sure Mikel pulled him to the side. He's 16 years old remember, he's still a kid. He's trying to set all sorts of records at the moment, and then he's got sent off as a 16-year-old.’

On whether he thought Neal’s tackle was dangerous, he said: ‘Well it's a challenge that happened all the time in my era, but obviously the rules have changed.

‘He’s gone for the ball but it’s a bit reckless. I thought Max was a little bit unlucky in what the scenario was, legs all tangled up in this way, but he reacted a little bit.

‘Usually, a referee just says, “OK, maybe a yellow card maximum” and that's it, done.’

Arsenal legend Ray Parlour believes the Gunners youngster was 'a little unlucky' to be sent off

Speaking at the premiere of the film ‘We Go Again’, the former midfielder also tipped Arteta to build a dynasty at Arsenal in a similar vein to Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden tenure at Manchester City.

‘Absolutely, he's got a great opportunity now to really, really dominate like Man City have done under Pep (Guardiola),’ he said.

‘He's got a great young squad of players. Everybody's going in the right direction, everybody knows they have to set their standards and he’s a very demanding manager which you've got to be with an elite team.

‘He’s done a brilliant job and people have given him time. Obviously, everybody's backed him including the owners.

‘We see with other managers, they come and go at clubs. Once you've got a good manager, you've got to try and stick with him. It’s great news that Mikel has signed a new contract, and obviously, players now will be signing new contracts as well. Hopefully they can stick together.’

#1684. Report: Liverpool star now a 'concrete option' for Euro giants

Liverpool still have a lot of work that needs to be done on their first-team squad.

The Anfield outfit are currently fifth in the Premier League table and, even though they've only lost two games across all competitions this season, some serious questions are being asked.

Most people thought that the Reds would be much better off without Arne Slot at the helm but, right now, they're in the exact same position they ended in last term.

Of course, a lot of new players have been brought in so it could take time for them to get used to how things work but, the fact that they barely played to the levels expected of them is massively concerning.

This is why fans are demanding change in the upcoming January transfer window with some of the Reds' players already being linked with moves away.

Inter Milan now see Federico Chiesa as a "concrete option" for them to explore

Inter Milan and Liverpool have been intertwined with many deals over the last few years.

The most recent negotiation between both clubs resulted in Curtis Jones joining the Italian giants for around £30 million.

On the face of things, this is an extremely low amount for a player of his quality but, since he had less than a year left on his contract and Liverpool had no intention of offering him a new deal, moving the Englishman on in the summer made a lot of sense.

Since then, Alessandro Bastoni has been linked with a Liverpool move and now, it seems like Inter have made Federico Chiesa one of their most-wanted targets.

"Federico Chiesa has emerged as a concrete option for Inter as they look to add a forward with a different profile to their attack," Ekrem Konur shared via X.

"The Italian international is appreciated for his experience, versatility and ability to offer something different in the final third.

"While no agreement has been reached, Chiesa remains firmly on the club's shortlist."

Liverpool must make their final decision on Federico Chiesa's future soon

Chiesa's time at Liverpool has been full of nothing but turmoil.

The Italian has barely played any football for the Reds and, even when he has, it's often been an appearance off the bench.

Of course, there have been games when he's started for Liverpool but, especially now that he's not a part of Liverpool's Champions League squad, it feels a bit pointless to keep the attacker around.

That is, even though Liverpool could certainly do with an upgrade or two in that department.

If the Anfield outfit don't make a decision about what they want to do with Chiesa soon, he's going to fade into obscurity and will probably just leave for free next year anyway.

So, if Inter come in with an offer, it feels like the best thing for Liverpool to do would be to accept it and either promote another youngster or sign a top-class player who can challenge for a starting position.

#1683. Barella admits Inter have changed derby approach in recent years: “We’re too inconsistent”

After the game, Nicolo Barella attempted to lessen the damage of last night’s loss to AC Milan in his post-game press conference.

For Milan, last night was another instance in what is becoming a new norm. After Inter’s streak of derby wins, it’s now the Rossoneri who are enjoying themselves. They’ve won each of their last four meetings and haven’t lost in eight games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In short, despite all of the managerial changes that have taken place, the Diavolo remain on top when it comes to playing the Nerazzurri.

Of course, last night’s win was also monumental considering what it meant for the Serie A table. Rather than falling 10 points behind, they only sit four points behind Inter and Lazio, who share first.

Speaking at a post-match conference, Barella admitted that Inter are going through a bad cycle in the derbies, but was keen to remember the streak from a few years ago, as MilanNews relayed.

“Certainly, if we talk about this, we’ve been lacking the ideal approach to matches since the start of the year. Right now, it’s a clear criticality for us.

“It’s true that we’ve shown our strength on many occasions, perhaps coming out on top in the second half or whenever we manage to break the deadlock, but it’s clear that not every match goes that way.

“We can’t expect to always repeat the same pattern, especially when we face a packed schedule with matches every three days. Fatigue, both physical and mental, is starting to take its toll, and we need to learn to manage matches better without being forced to keep them in the balance until the ninetieth minute.”

Is there a feeling that, whatever you do, Milan will prevail in derbies?

“Let’s say I’ve also experienced it the other way around. I’ve had a lot of derby wins in a row, so I don’t know if it’s a cyclical thing, but it’s definitely a game we haven’t approached in the best way in recent years, recently.

“There have been derbies where we’ve played well and lost, where we’ve played poorly and maybe drawn, but we’re too inconsistent in derbies, and right now, even in important matches. Even though we won, we still needed to do better.”

Do you still have the fierce desire to prove that you are the strongest?

“Being the strongest is sometimes not enough, because we’ve also been the strongest team, or the one everyone thought was the strongest, but then we didn’t win. So right now, I think we need to focus on something else rather than our strength.

“It’s true that if we look back at the last few games, many goals come from individual errors, and we need to improve on those, each of us, because unfortunately, individual errors work against the team. But as a team, we need to improve a bit in terms of solidity, which is what has always set us apart, what got us to the Champions League final, what helped us win the Scudetto, and perhaps right now we’re not the best version of ourselves. So we need to work on that. We still have the desire to win, for sure, because that’s what keeps us going to the pitch every day and motivates us, but we need to improve.”

#1682. Liverpool transfer news: Two ‘major targets’ identified as Reds ‘accelerate’ defensive rebuild

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 12:56, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 12:58

Liverpool have stepped up their plans for a major defensive rebuild in 2027, according to a report.

The Reds have only kept four clean sheets in 14 matches across all competitions this season since the arrival of new head coach Andoni Iraola.

Captain Virgil van Dijk remains at the heart of Liverpool’s defence, but the 35-year-old is out of contract next summer and it remains to be seen whether he will renew his deal.

Joe Gomez has also entered the final year of his contract at Anfield, and bolstering the centre-back department is becoming a priority for the Merseysiders heading into the New Year.

According to the Daily Briefing, via Caught Offside, Borussia Dortmund’s Nico Schlotterbeck and Nottingham Forest’s Murillo are two major central defensive targets on Liverpool’s wishlist.

While a formal offer is yet to have been submitted for either player, it is understood that Liverpool are in the process of scouting and performance analysis, while they are also assessing the conditions that would be required for future negotiations.

Schlotterbeck, who has been linked with Liverpool for more than 12 months, committed his future to Dortmund in April by signing a new contract until the summer of 2031.

The 26-year-old’s new deal is said to include a release clause worth between €50m (£41.8m) and €60m (£50.1m) for selected clubs, while Dortmund would entertain offers of around €70m (£58.5m) for other teams.

Schlotterbeck has established himself as an integral first-team defender for Dortmund and has developed his leadership skills while wearing the captain’s armband for all eight of his appearances in the 2026-27 season in the absence of injured skipper Emre Can.

The Germany international’s aggression in duels, aerial presence, left-footed distribution and ability to step into midfield are all believed to be qualities that appeal to Liverpool.

Murillo, meanwhile, is also a powerful left-footed player who combines his explosive recovery pace with aggressive one-on-one defending and confidence progressing the ball out from the back.

The 24-year-old is a proven Premier League centre-back who has spent three-and-a-half years at Nottingham Forest, making 102 top-flight appearances.

Forest are said to have no intention of parting ways with Murillo – a one-cap Brazil international – during the January transfer window.

Murillo is under contract at the City Ground until June 2030 and an ‘enormous offer’ would be required for Forest to entertain his departure in the near future.

Meanwhile, Liverpool are also said to hold an interest in Inter Milan’s Alessandro Bastoni and Barcelona’s Jules Kounde, while they still have the option to make Ronald Araujo’s loan move from Camp Nou permanent for £47m next summer.

#1681. Report: Liverpool eyeing move for perfect Premier League sensation

Liverpool have had a bit of a topsy-turvy season thus far.

Andoni Iraola is obviously still trying to figure out who his best starting XI are but, with Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley still likely to be out for a while, it's unclear when he's actually going to sort out who his preferred XI are.

And, with the January transfer window now not all that far away, even more changes could be afoot.

This is obviously exciting but, since they've already spent over £600 million across the last couple of seasons, it's unclear how much money Iraola and Julian Ward will actually have to spend.

#1680. Man United vs. Roma: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Champions League clash

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 13:13, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 13:14

Manchester United will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with a clash against Roma on Tuesday night.

The 20-time English champions desperately need a positive result, but they will be welcoming a Roma side with four wins from their last five matches during a strong run of form.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Champions League match will kick off at 8pm UK time on Tuesday.

The Champions League match between Man United and Roma will be played at the English club's home stadium, Old Trafford.

The last clash between the two teams at Old Trafford came in the quarter-finals of the 2007-08 Champions League, with Man United recording a 1-0 victory to secure a 3-0 aggregate success and progress to the semi-finals.

The European game will not be broadcast live on TV in the UK.

The Champions League clash can be streamed live on Amazon's Prime Video.

Game-changing events will be posted on the PrimeVideoSport X account, while highlights will be uploaded to the Amazon Prime Video Sport YouTube channel later in the evening.

It has to turn for Man United at some point; the Red Devils are now nine games without a win in all competitions and have lost four of their last five during a horrendous run.

Michael Carrick has kept his job at the helm for now, but two more poor results against Roma and Aston Villa would surely see a change in the dug-out.

Man United are 20th in the overall Champions League table with three points from three matches, while Roma sit in 15th on four points.

Roma have won four of their last five matches during a strong run of form and will therefore enter this game full of confidence against a fragile Red Devils outfit.

#1679. McInnes claims Fernandez has become an easy target for critics as he backs under-fire defender

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 14:38 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EDT, 29 October 2026

RANGERS boss Derek McInnes has launched an impassioned defence of Manny Fernandez — claiming that the defender has become an easy target for criticism.

Fernandez came under fire for his performance in the 2-2 draw away at Hearts on Wednesday night, with a large section of the support believing he should now be dropped.

The 25-year-old centre-back has been error-prone for much of the season, despite being the preferred partner for Olwethu Makhanya in central defence.

Speaking to the BBC, Rangers legend Ian Ferguson branded Fernandez’s performance at Tynecastle as ‘woeful’ and insisted he should have been taken off in the first half.

With Ben Godfrey now fit again, there are calls for McInnes to drop Fernandez and reinstate the former England international for Saturday’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final against Aberdeen at Hampden.

But McInnes leapt to the defence of Fernandez yesterday and insisted that the scrutiny on his performances only becomes an issue when Rangers have dropped points.

Fernandez has been a regular at the heart of Rangers' defence so far this season

‘I only get asked about Fernandez when he has a poor game,’ said the Rangers boss. ‘Nobody asked me about Fernandez last Saturday against St Johnstone [in a 4-0 win].

‘He was outstanding. He looked like he could have played St Johnstone himself at the back. So, I understand when players drop because he’s got such a high ceiling and when he’s good, he’s very good.

‘But that’s the same for a lot of players. Last night against Hearts wasn’t on Manny Fernandez, it was a collective.

‘I never get asked about Manny when he does really well and he’s been a big part of our better performances this season.’

Pressed on whether he now has a decision to make with Godfrey fit again, McInnes said: ‘I’ve got loads of decisions to make across the team.

‘I think it’s important that we’ve been pretty consistent and we’ve been pretty good with results. I know the Hearts game was not perfect. The last two away games we’ve drawn, but we’re still unbeaten on the road.

‘We’re still being pretty strong. Our record’s been, well, not brilliant, but our unbeaten run has gone on a while now.

‘I think that while we recognise that individuals can play better last night, we’ve got decisions to make across the board, particularly when there’s three games in the week.’

McInnes saw his side narrowly avoid defeat on his return to Tynecastle on Wednesday night

McInnes revealed that midfielder Tochi Chukwuani could be set for a spell out of action after picking up a knee injury against Hearts.

Rangers will start as heavy favourites at Hampden against an Aberdeen side who are badly out of form under Stephen Robinson.

Robinson is under huge pressure and there are some suggestions that his job could be on the line if Aberdeen lose against their bitter rivals.

As a former Aberdeen manager himself, McInnes recognises the pressure that comes with the job at Pittodrie. But he is determined to continue his own quest to clinch the first piece of silverware of the season, something which he feels would bring a huge psychological boost to his players.

‘I think a semi-final, a stand-alone game, sometimes form goes out the window,’ said the Rangers boss. ‘Aberdeen have got a good, experienced manager in Robbo and got some good, experienced players.

‘They’ll be relishing the opportunity as well. People might view us as favourites for it and I understand that, but we’ve still got a game to win and Aberdeen are capable of a big performance.

‘I’m just concentrating on us. If we get to our levels, then hopefully it’s going to be enough to win the game. But a strong 90-minute performance is going to be required.

Ben Godfrey's return to fitness has led to some fans calling for him to replace Fernandez

‘I know things have maybe not been going great for Aberdeen lately, but we can’t focus too much on that.

‘I sympathise with all the managers who feel that pressure. I’ve managed the club for eight years up there and it’s not always an easy club to manage. But they’ve got a good guy there and a guy who will get it right if given time. I have no doubts about it.

‘From our own point of view, I think supporters, players, staff alike, for everybody connected with the club to get the first trophy would be so important.

‘Obviously, we had a tough tie to navigate last time round, beating Celtic. Now we’re in a semi-final, it’s important that you turn up.

‘Semi-finals, traditionally, can be fraught with a lot of nerves and tension. Sometimes they are not the best games because of what’s at stake, but we can’t just turn up on Saturday hoping to win. We’ve just got to go out and set about the task.

‘It’s something that’s very important to us all, to try and make sure we get to the final. But there is a team who will be equally as determined to get there as well.’

#1678. Report: Liverpool are now ready to sign 'incredible' €45m defender

Liverpool's defence have caused some questions to arise this season.

Whether they've failed to meet expectations or made a massive mistake, several questions have been shared about what the future holds for them.

At the moment, Virgil van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo all have their positions in Andoni Iraola's starting XI fairly locked down but, left-back is a completely different story.

Both Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez have failed to meet expectations and have made multiple mistakes each this term.

Obviously, this is far from ideal, especially for a team who want to challenge for as many titles as possible.

So, the fact that Liverpool now look ready to sign a new defender is ideal.

Liverpool are ready to go 'all out' for Alejandro Balde

Full-back has been a problem for Liverpool over the last couple of years.

The Anfield outfit lost Trent Alexander-Arnold last summer with Andy Robertson also following him out of the exit doors this summer.

This, coupled with the fact that Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong are both constantly injured causes a major problem for Liverpool.

That's why these latest links from journalist Juan Jesus make a lot of sense.

"Liverpool and AC Milan are going all out for Alejandro Balde. They join Manchester United in the bidding war," he wrote.

"Both Andoni Iraola and Rúben Amorim are fans of the player and believe he would fit perfectly into their respective systems.

"Already open to leaving this winter, Barça has already set his price: the Catalan club is asking for a minimum of 45 million euros to let him go."

Alejandro Balde is a perfect signing for Liverpool

Alejandro Balde is a player who's been linked with Liverpool a lot over the last couple of months.

The left-back has fallen out of favour with Hansi Flick at Barcelona and, because of this, the La Liga giants seem to be willing to get rid of him for a cut-rate fee.

And, while he may be a natural left-back, he's also been used as a right-back in the past which is especially good for Liverpool and their injury prone defenders.

Balde is also only 23 years old so, even though he's already a top notch player, there's plenty of time left in his career for him to become even better.

At the moment, these are all obviously just rumours but, if Liverpool are ready to go all out for the "incredible" left-back, the deal could very well be on.

#1676. Man United head coach Michael Carrick confirms Patrick Dorgu decision for Roma clash as 22-year-old makes timely return

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 13:45, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 13:47

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said that Patrick Dorgu will not be involved in Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma despite returning to training.

Dorgu has missed Man United's last six matches due to an injury that he sustained while representing Denmark during the September/October international break.

The 22-year-old was pictured back in training on Monday, though, fuelling rumours that a return to the squad against Roma was possible.

Carrick has confirmed that the Dane is not yet ready to return to action, but there is a chance that he could be involved against Aston Villa in the Premier League this weekend.

"Yeah, it was his first day with the group, great to have him back, but he won't be involved tomorrow. We'll see how he progresses for the week (for Villa)," Carrick told reporters.

Dorgu's return is timely given Man United's issues at left-back, with Luke Shaw still unavailable for selection.

Man United will also again be missing Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford against Roma, while Manuel Ugarte is a long-term absentee for the 20-time English champions.

Lisandro Martinez is available, as his upcoming ban only relates to domestic matches, but it remains to be seen whether the Argentina international starts following his red card in the team's 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday afternoon.

When asked about possible concerns surrounding Martinez's commitment, Carrick said: "I've got no concerns about commitment at all. Things happen in football, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but commitment is not an issue, for sure."

Carrick remains under major pressure due to the team's struggles this season. Indeed, the Red Devils are without a victory in their last nine games in all competitions.

"I know the players, I know what we’re capable of as a team… we’ve showed it in spells, showed it in bursts," Carrick added during his pre-Roma press conference.

Defeats to Roma and Aston Villa in the team's next two matches would likely spell the end of Carrick's time at the helm, but there is still an opportunity for the club's former midfielder to turn the campaign around.

#1675. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

Liverpool's performances this season have been a tad ropey.

And, while Liverpool weren't the favourites going into that game, they still should have done better than they did.

Liverpool may want to sign Morgan Gibbs-White as their Florian Wirtz replacement

This season, things don't seem to have changed all that much and, even though Wirtz is being used in his preferred position of number 10, he's still failing to meet expectations.

Because of this, rumours have started to emerge with Liverpool even being linked with a move for Morgan Gibbs-White ahead of the January transfer window.

"Morgan Gibbs-White is considered one of the most attainable attacking midfield options for Manchester United," Ekrem Konur wrote.

"Interest in the Nottingham Forest star remains strong, with Tottenham and Liverpool also keeping a close eye on his situation.

Morgan Gibbs-White would be a perfect transfer for Liverpool

Whether Liverpool believe that midfield or defence is their biggest problem, change has to occur.

Of all the recent links that have emerged about Liverpool. Gibbs-White makes a lot of sense.

#1673. Michael Olise vs. Eberechi Eze: How two Palace standouts took such different paths at Arsenal and Bayern Munich

By Axel Clody | 02 Nov 2026 13:55

The Frenchman has become the creative reference point for the Bavarian giants, while the Englishman is still looking for his place at Arsenal.

Michael Olise and Eberechi Eze left Crystal Palace at different times, but they shared something: they had established themselves as two of the most talented players at the club. The Frenchman went to Bayern Munich in 2024, while the Englishman fulfilled his dream of playing for Arsenal a year later.

Since then, their trajectories have taken different directions, showing how tactical context and space within a team can be decisive for a player’s development.

Olise turned the potential he showed in England into a leading role in Germany. Since arriving at Bayern Munich, the attacker has become one of the team’s main offensive creators, combining goals, assists and constant involvement in build-up play. Ninth place in the 2026 Ballon d’Or recognised an evolution that was already evident on the pitch, although a higher position would have been fairer.

Eze, on the other hand, has not yet been able to reproduce the influence he had at Palace at Arsenal. Signed to add creativity and the ability to unbalance the attack, the midfielder alternates between performances out wide and opportunities as an alternative to Martin Odegaard. The change of role, together with the competition for places, helps explain why his adaptation is far from achieving the same success as his former team-mate.

Michael Olise’s numbers in Germany show a progression that goes beyond a good run in front of goal. In his first season at Bayern Munich, in 2024-25, the Frenchman scored 20 goals and provided 20 assists in 55 games. The following campaign, he maintained his consistency and raised his output to 21 goals and 26 assists in 52 games. At the start of 2026-27, he already has 10 goals and five assists in just 11 appearances.

The number of direct goal contributions is striking, but it does not explain the attacker’s importance on its own. Olise is a player capable of taking responsibility for finishing a move or identifying the team-mate in a better position to finish it. His repertoire includes passes that break defensive lines, accurate crosses, combinations in tight spaces and individual moves that force opponents to shift their marking.

That variety makes him a true playmaker, even when playing mainly on the flanks.

Olise does not need to receive the ball in a position to shoot to be decisive: he can also drop back a few metres, take part in circulation and speed up the attack with a pass that disorganises the defence. When he finds space to carry the ball towards the box, he adds a constant goal threat to that creative ability.

Bayern Munich’s context also favours this repertoire. In a team that often takes control of matches and has attackers capable of getting into the box, Olise finds options to turn his vision into assists. The presence of team-mates who move to receive his passes widens the possibilities for combinations and prevents opposition marking from focusing exclusively on blocking his shots.

That does not mean the Frenchman has become a different player from the one at Crystal Palace. In England, he already showed technical quality, vision and the ability to decide matches. The difference is in the dimension those characteristics have reached in Munich.

Bayern Munich offers a bigger stage, but Olise has also risen to the demands, improving his consistency and his ability to influence different moments of matches.

Eberechi Eze’s trajectory is more complex because his difficulty is not limited to attacking production. In 2024-25, his last full season at Crystal Palace, the midfielder scored 15 goals and provided 11 assists in 43 games. He was one of the main sources of the team’s creativity, with the freedom to receive between the lines, carry the ball and get close to the box. His performances justified Arsenal’s interest, and they signed him in 2025.

His first season at Arsenal, however, left a less impressive record than the raw numbers may suggest. Eze scored 10 goals and provided five assists in 52 games in 2025-26.

They are reasonable statistics for a player who had to adapt to a new team, but the distribution of the goals deserves attention: five of them came in just two north London derbies against Tottenham, both in the Premier League. In one of those games he scored a hat-trick, in the other he found the net twice.

Those two games helped build his image as a tormentor of Tottenham, but they also show why the total goal count is not enough to judge his season. Outside those matches, Eze was unable to maintain a frequency of decisive contributions that would put him among Arsenal’s main attacking references.

The problem is not to disregard the importance of scoring in derbies, but to recognise that one-off great performances do not replace the constant influence expected of a player signed to add creativity to the team.

The tactical question is central. At Palace, Eze played in a system with three centre-backs and two wing-backs, the 3-4-3, which allowed him to occupy inside areas often and take part directly in creation. At Arsenal, his use has been more variable. In some games he appears out wide; in others he appears as an alternative to Odegaard, who occupies an important central role in the team’s offensive organisation.

The difference is not only in the starting position. When he receives further from the box, Eze has to beat his marker in situations where he has fewer passing options nearby. Inside, he can make better use of his carrying, his ability to turn under pressure and his vision to find team-mates. At the same time, competing with Odegaard means competing for a position in which Arsenal already have an established player in the collective structure.

The start of 2026-27 reinforces the difficulty of gaining continuity. Eze has two goals and one assist in 12 games in all competitions. In the first eight Premier League rounds, he started only twice, came on from the bench in another four and did not leave the bench in the other two. With fewer minutes and alternating roles, it is harder to gain rhythm, build understanding and establish a run of performances capable of changing his situation.

The comparison with Olise, therefore, should not be read as a definitive verdict on Eze’s quality. The two arrived at their new clubs in different circumstances and found different demands. The Frenchman gained space to turn his creativity into a central weapon for Bayern Munich; the Englishman still needs to find a role in which he can take more part in build-up and receive the ball in the zones where he performs best.

The talent that made Eze one of Palace’s standouts has not disappeared. The question is how to use it in an Arsenal side with an offensive structure different from the one he was used to. Olise has already found that answer at Bayern Munich and become one of the team’s most influential names. Eze is still looking for his, and until he wins space and consistency, the gap between the two trajectories is likely to remain evident.

#1672. Jude Bellingham's father Mark called up to play for England's OVER-50s in clash with Ireland - after smashing more than 700 goals during journeyman non-league career

Published: 15:12 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EDT, 29 October 2026

Jude Bellingham's father Mark has received a call up to England Veterans Over 50s squad to face Republic of Ireland this weekend.

A talented non-league striker in his heyday, Bellingham netted over 700 goals across at least 20 different clubs, including Leamington, Stourbridge and Sutton Coldfield Town.

He even earned the nickname the 'Non-League Pele' during his 25-year career, which ended in 2017.

The father of Real Madrid and England superstar Jude, 23, and Borussia Dortmund and England Under-23 midfielder Jobe, Mark is now set to dust off his shooting boots and become the third member of the Bellingham family to don the Three Lions shirt.

England Veterans Over 50s are the reigning Seniors World Cup champions, having clinched their ninth title in Thailand earlier this year.

Gareth Barry, the former Manchester City and Everton midfielder, lined up for the side alongside Lee Hendrie, also formerly of Aston Villa, although both of those names are absent for the upcoming match in Berkshire on Sunday, November 1.

The father of Real Madrid superstar Jude, 23, and Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe, Mark is now set to dust off his shooting boots (Source: judebellingham/Instagram)

A former West Midlands Police officer, Bellingham earned the nickname the 'Non-League Pele' during his 25-year career. Pictured above with Jude (Source: CJPhillips1982/X)

When not playing football of his own, Bellingham is regularly seen attending his two sons' matches.

A Southend United supporter, Mark introduced Jude to football, with the England star's first live matches coming alongside his father at Roots Hall.

Speaking about his father in a recent interview, Jude said: 'We talk about footballing heroes, and my dad was like my first.

'When you go and watch him play every week in non-league, you know it's not the Premier League or anything, but seeing the way that he played and the atmosphere, it made me fall in love with football so he was probably my first hero.

'After the first few times of going, I'd start to pay a bit more attention to the games and stuff, the atmosphere and he's scoring goals so you see him celebrating and stuff like that - you want that to be me.

'Growing up, he'd always give me tips on what I could do and now it gets to a certain age and it sort of flips and that's brilliant because we have that sort of relationship like father and son and then as I got older, like coach and player.'

Mark helped set up Stourbridge Juniors, Jude’s first club, and was a sergeant before fully focusing on his sons’ careers.

He became their agent and negotiated Jude’s £88.5m transfer to Real Madrid from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, and dealt with Dortmund again when Jobe moved there from Sunderland in 2025.

Mark and Jude and Jobe's mother, Denise, are understood to have separated but remain close, the pair having attended Jude's games at the World Cup together this past summer

While in Germany, Mark reportedly held an emotional discussion with Dortmund sporting director Sebastian Kehl after being left unhappy by Jobe's substitution at half-time during his Bundesliga debut.

German publication BILD added at the time that Mark sought a meeting with manager Niko Kovac directly - and 'made no secret of his opinion.' The club proceeded to ban all family members from the dressing room following the incident.

Mark’s influence as an agent is said to have stretched to Jude’s media duties when with England. Notably, the player has gone out of his way to speak more at this most recent World Cup, but at previous tournaments he had avoided speaking beyond his obligations despite his increasing influence within the squad.

Mark and Jude and Jobe's mother, Denise, are understood to have separated but remain close, the pair having attended Jude's games at the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico this past summer.

#1670. Man United head coach Michael Carrick addresses fresh speculation surrounding his future ahead of fascinating Roma showdown

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 14:00, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 14:03

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said that he "can't wait" for Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils are without a victory in their last nine matches in all competitions, and there is major pressure on Carrick during an incredibly difficult period for the club.

Man United have lost four of their last five matches, including each of their last three, but Carrick is still convinced that he is the right man for the job.

The 20-time English champions will play two more fixtures ahead of the November international break, hosting Roma in Europe, before welcoming Aston Villa to Old Trafford in the Premier League this weekend.

When asked whether he feels as if he has only two more games at the helm, Carrick said: "No, not at all. You you never know what is going to happen in the future, but that doesn't change the way I feel.

"I can't wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had, but I can't wait for it.

"The dressing room is in a good place. Perception is a funny thing, you can make things look in different ways. The commitment from the players, to the club and each other, I don't question that at all.

"It's what I am, it's what I live for, a lot of people could do my job when you're winning games. It hasn't changed my mindset (bad results)."

Carrick had been widely expected to lose his job off the back of Man United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth in the Premier League on October 25.

The Englishman led the Red Devils into Saturday's game at Chelsea, and while it was a much-improved performance, Man United lost again.

The 20-time English champions will play five times in November, facing Liverpool in their first match after the upcoming international break, before tackling Sporting Lisbon and Brentford.

Eddie Howe remains the favourite to replace Carrick at the helm, should Man United make a change in the dug-out.

#1668. Blackburn Rovers vs Stoke City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 02 Nov 2026 14:12, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 17:02

After facing Welsh opposition in successive weekends, Blackburn Rovers will be looking to return to winning ways in the Championship on Tuesday night when they welcome in-form Stoke City to Ewood Park.

Rovers were thrashed by high-flying Swansea City in South Wales at the weekend and will be eager to put that 4-0 defeat behind them, while the Potters returned to winning ways after a goalless draw with Bristol City by beating Preston North End 2-0 to round off a successful October in style.

Having narrowly avoided relegation to League One last season, Blackburn Rovers turned to former manager Tony Mowbray in the summer, hoping the 62-year-old could guide the Lancashire club further up the table.

After 13 Championship matches back at the club where he oversaw 267 games between February 2017 and May 2022, Mowbray has made a positive start, with five wins, three draws and five defeats leaving Rovers 13th in the table and nine points clear of the relegation zone.

Blackburn have faced all three Welsh sides in the Championship this month, with victories over Cardiff City and Wrexham helping them move further away from danger, but a heavy 4-0 defeat to promotion hopefuls Swansea on Saturday prevented them from making it three such wins in a row.

Mowbray's side travelled across the border just two points outside the top eight, having won four of their previous six league outings, but goals from Stephen Eustaquio, Joseph Opoku and Filip Lissah in the first half, followed by Ross Stewart's strike shortly before the hour mark, condemned Rovers to their heaviest defeat of the campaign.

A victory on Tuesday against a side they have failed to beat in their last four meetings could leave Blackburn just one point outside the playoff places heading into the weekend, underlining the progress they have made after finishing 20th and only five points above the bottom three last season.

As for Stoke City, they make the 70-mile journey north looking to build on an excellent start to the campaign, having defied expectations after ending last season in the bottom half of the table.

Under Mark Robins, the Potters have made their best start to a Championship season since being relegated from the Premier League in 2018, collecting seven wins, two draws and four defeats from their opening 13 matches to sit seventh with 23 points.

Stoke began the 2026-27 campaign with three successive defeats but have since turned their fortunes around following a 4-1 thrashing by Wolverhampton Wanderers at the end of August.

A change in formation, with Robins now favouring a back three, has helped spark an impressive run of seven wins in their last 10 matches, with their only defeat during that period coming against league leaders Middlesbrough, who snatched a 91st-minute winner.

Since the start of September, no side has conceded fewer goals than Robins' men, highlighting the impact of their reshaped young defence at the bet365 Stadium, while a 2-0 victory over bottom club Preston North End at the weekend was secured through goals from Ben Wilmot and Jack McGlynn.

The sides meet for the first time this season, having drawn 1-1 in each of their last two encounters.

Following a 4-0 defeat last time out, Mowbray may have been considering changes regardless, but further injury problems mean he will have little choice but to freshen up his side for Tuesday's clash.

Harry Pickering was forced off after just 24 minutes against Swansea and will miss this match, with Gady Beyuku having replaced him at the time and now in contention to start against the Potters.

The full-back will join Adam Forshaw and Ryoya Morishita on the sidelines, although the midfield duo are closing in on returns to action.

On a more positive note, Yuri Ribeiro and Yuki Ohashi are both be available for selection after returning to the bench last time out, having missed the previous month and eight weeks respectively.

As for the visitors, Robins has the option of naming an unchanged side, although the quick turnaround between fixtures could prompt some alterations.

Stoke will be without Eric Bocat, Ato Ampah, Sam Gallagher and Lamine Cisse, but captain Viktor Johansson is expected to retain his place in goal, while American winger McGlynn is also likely to feature after netting for the third time in the league on Saturday.

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:

B. Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Baradji, Montgomery; Fevrier, Cantwell; Afolayan; Gudjohnsen

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Soumare, Galbraith, Bombino; McGlynn, Bozenik, Devenny

Although both sides have made far more encouraging starts to the new season than many of their supporters might have anticipated, we expect Stoke to come away from Ewood Park with all three points on Tuesday night.

The Potters will be keen to extend their unbeaten run to four matches, and we believe they can do so by claiming an eighth league victory of the campaign and moving closer to the automatic promotion places.

The Reds learned that the hard way last summer when Marc Guehi looked destined to join, only for Palace to pull the plug at the eleventh hour, despite the defender already wearing Liverpool training gear.

History repeated itself this summer when Liverpool failed to land Ismaila Sarr. Palace demanded £75m for the Senegalese winger, a fee that simply wasn't feasible for the Reds.

That leaves Liverpool's hopes of signing Wharton hanging in the balance. If Palace remain this stubborn, securing his signature could prove another costly and complicated saga.

Liverpool's need to buy a midfielder explainedWith or without Wharton, the Reds do have to have some big preparations for the future of their midfield. The defence and the attack have undergone a transformation in the last couple of transfer windows. It feels like both are well-set up for the future with only a couple of additions missing. That's the opposite for the midfield where uncertainty looms. Alexis Mac Allister has been in great form but right now his fellow midfielders, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch are struggling. Ironically it's Mac Allister who doesn't know whether he is going to be offered a contract extension whereas the other two are already on long-term deals. There's talk Liverpool could already be making their move to sign Lamine Camara in the January window.

With or without Wharton, the Reds do have to have some big preparations for the future of their midfield.

The defence and the attack have undergone a transformation in the last couple of transfer windows. It feels like both are well-set up for the future with only a couple of additions missing.

That's the opposite for the midfield where uncertainty looms. Alexis Mac Allister has been in great form but right now his fellow midfielders, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch are struggling.

Ironically it's Mac Allister who doesn't know whether he is going to be offered a contract extension whereas the other two are already on long-term deals. There's talk Liverpool could already be making their move to sign Lamine Camara in the January window.

But what if Liverpool don't even need to enter the transfer market? In the last few weeks, Trey Nyoni is making it abundantly clear that the Reds can find their solutions from within.

Over the last few games, Nyoni has emerged as one of Liverpool's best players. His composure on the ball and ability to send line-breaking passes are outstanding.

It's exactly what the Reds have wanted in their midfield since the departure of Thiago and Fabinho. It's why Wharton has been sought out by the club.

But Nyoni might just be the answer instead. He made 14 line-breaking passes against Arsenal and 11 passes into the opposition's final third.

Those are Wharton esque numbers, and the fact that he did it against the Champions of the Premier League proves that Nyoni has arrived.

#1666. Unbeaten run, a rare free-kick and more: All the key stats from AC Milan 3-1 Inter

As is often the case with the derby win, there were a lot of fun facts and stats to delve into after the full-time whistle, including a free-kick rarity from Diego Moreira.

Many headed into the Derby della Madonnina with a lot of worry considering Inter’s strong start to the season, as well as Milan’s mid-week defeat to Bologna. However, it turned out to be a great evening for the Rossoneri, who clinched all three points in a 3-1 win.

Diego Moreira played a key role in the success, bagging one goal and two assists, while Ruben Amorim got his tactics right as well. In short, it was just what they needed and as is often the case after a huge win, a lot of fun stats emerged afterwards.

Starting with the general stats, it’s clear that Milan made the most of their chances with a 0.66 xG and three goals scored. Moreira’s free-kick obviously didn’t yield a high xG, nor did Adrien Rabiot’s tidy effort, and Christian Pulisic’s header wasn’t super easy to pull off.

Inter had some good chances from close range, parried by Mike Maignan, so that is probably why their xG is higher. Alessandro Bastoni’s header was also an easy one, unlike Pulisic’s, but it was nice to see Milan be the efficient team for once.

The possession is linked to the above, really, as Milan sat back a lot after scoring their goals. Tactically, they played it to perfection and Inter didn’t really create much with all that possession in the end.

This deserves a section of its own because Milan’s recent record in the derby is truly amazing. After losing six games on the trot, the Rossoneri have certainly turned things around with six wins in the last eight encounters and no defeats!

Now the Inter fans can feel some of the pain that we experienced a while back… It’s not just that the Nerazzurri as a club have been really poor against Milan, it’s also that Cristian Chivu has failed completely.

Winning trophies is the most important thing, he’s absolutely right, but there is no question that the derby record is bothering him. As reported by Opta, he’s only the third manager to lose his first three derbies after Leonardo (2009-2011) and Massimo Giacomini (1979-1980).

Like we said at the start, a lot of fun facts emerged from the win last night and giving each of them a section would be a little silly. From a rare free-kick goal in the derby to a midfielder in red-hot form, we have listed them below.

Moreira’s free-kick: Since Opta started collecting the stats in 2004-05, Milan have only scored three direct free-kick goals against Inter in all competitions, with Moreira’s being the latest one. Pirlo (2007) and Theo Hernandez (2025) were the first two.

Pulisic’s speedy start: Pulisic’s goal is the fastest Milan have scored in a league derby against Inter since the 2010-11 season, when Alexandre Pato found the back of the net after a mere 43 seconds. Talk about getting off the right foot.

Rabiot’s goal contributions: Rabiot has become the third Milan midfielder to have at least one goal contribution in five consecutive league games since 2004-05, following in the footsteps of Hakan Calhanoglu (in 2020) and Ricky Kaka (2004 and 2008).

#1665. AEK Athens vs. Real Madrid: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of Champions League clash

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 14:42, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 14:43

Real Madrid will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with a clash against Greek outfit AEK Athens on Wednesday night.

Los Blancos are fourth in the overall Champions League table, picking up nine points from three matches, while AEK Athens are 29th in the division, collecting three points from their three games in the league stage this term.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides ahead of Wednesday's fixture in Athens.

Real Madrid and AEK Athens have locked horns on four previous occasions throughout history, and both teams have posted one victory, while there have been two draws.

The first two meetings between the two teams came in the UEFA Cup back in 1985; AEK Athens recorded a 1-0 victory in the first leg of their first-round fixture, but Real Madrid were 5-0 winners in the second leg to secure a 5-1 aggregate success.

The pair then locked horns in the group stage of the 2002-03 Champions League, and both of those fixtures finished level - a 3-3 draw in Athens before a 2-2 at Bernabeu.

Real Madrid will be bidding to record a first-ever away victory over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

Incredibly, Los Blancos have won only one of their eight UEFA away games against Greek opposition, drawing five times in the process.

Oct 22, 2002: Real Madrid 2-2 AEK Athens (Champions League Group Stage)

Oct 02, 2002: AEK Athens 3-3 Real Madrid (Champions League Group Stage)

Oct 02, 1985: Real Madrid 5-0 AEK Athens (UEFA Cup First Round)

Sept 18, 1985: AEK Athens 1-0 Real Madrid (UEFA Cup First Round)

Oct 22, 2002: Real Madrid 2-2 AEK Athens (Champions League Group Stage)

Oct 02, 2002: AEK Athens 3-3 Real Madrid (Champions League Group Stage)

#1664. The real reasons it's all gone wrong for Kasper Hogh at Celtic... and why the Danish striker looks like a fish out of water away from Bodo/Glimt

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 14:17 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 15:22 EDT, 29 October 2026

Even for someone who radiates positivity the way he seems to each day, Kasper Hogh must have found the second half of Celtic’s match with Dundee United a tough watch.

Not so much the improved second-half performance from Martin O’Neill’s side which yielded a point, but the fact that it came following his removal from the fray at the interval.

You’d have needed a heart of stone not to have felt a pang of sympathy for the Dane as a 13th game in a Celtic jersey came and went without him finding the back of the net.

Having teed up Camilo Duran for the opening goal, Hogh’s hopes of seeing his own name go up in lights ended after 45 minutes of profound frustration.

Even the player’s growing band of critics would have to concede that the Dane was – to some extent – a victim of circumstances on the night.

O’Neill began the match with his wide positions filled by Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran – both fine players in their own rights – but centre-forwards to trade.

The sight of £11million striker Kasper Hogh warming the bench at Celtic has become the norm

Accordingly, the service into Hogh from the flanks was patchy. You can question the player’s touch and his movement in the box all you like. He cannot be held responsible for crosses being stopped at source.

It was a different story in the second half, or, at least, it might have been from Hogh’s perspective had O’Neill not kept him indoors.

With Jota and Haissem Hassan introduced, the kind of deliveries Hogh would have been praying for arrived after he’d taken a shower.

While you can understand O’Neill’s logic in moving Duran infield to his preferred role after seeing him score his 11th goal of the season, Hogh became the fall guy for the grand plan and another match came and went without him scoring.

‘He played a part,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I thought he worked exceptionally hard for us again. One or two things that he tried maybe didn’t come off. But, overall, he’s made the goal.

‘That will give him a boost of confidence. We put on two wide players and I’m sure he’s probably frustrated that he’s sitting out and not playing a part in the second half.’

Hogh set up Camilo Duran for Celtic's opener against Dundee Utd but was hooked at half-time

The trouble for Hogh is that opportunities to change the narrative are only going to diminish in the coming weeks.

Duran was often played out wide earlier in the campaign out of sheer necessity, but Celtic’s options on the wings have improved recently and will only continue to do so.

Jota is nearing the point where he can start matches. Hassan already can. Hyun-jun Yang resumes training next week. James Forrest and Seb Tounekti are still in the building.

That reduces the likelihood of Duran and/or Osmand being deployed as they were initially against United. It increases the possibility of Celtic’s record signing finding himself as second or third choice striker.

Such a scenario would have felt preposterous when he took the acclaim of the visiting support at Rugby Park on August 9 with the match ball jammed under his arm. To say he looked the part that day would be a gross understatement.

Scoring with a header from Arne Engels’ cross inside two minutes, Hogh side-footed home Benjamin Nygren’s square ball then smartly made space to nod home Duran’s cross to wrap up a hat-trick inside 35 minutes.

Hogh has now gone 13 games without a goal and fans are becoming increasingly concerned

What was noticeable that day was that Celtic spent the entire game playing to Hogh’s strengths – crosses and cut-backs – as he stood between the width of the posts.

Despite his height, there seemed a recognition from those around him that he was a penalty box player as opposed to a target man. That necessitated a bespoke approach.

Yet, for reasons only they or the coaching staff could explain, Hogh’s team-mates often dispensed with that tactic in many of the key matches which followed.

In Linz, as Celtic wilted against LASK, and at Ibrox, as they capitulated against Rangers, the ball was repeatedly shelled up to the Dane. What did they expect to happen?

This brainless breakout of industrial football did neither the player nor the side any favours.

With the likes of Tounekti providing pitiful service from out wide, Hogh began to leave his station in search of the ball. Frequently, he was posted missing when the sought-after crosses occasionally arrived.

Celtic looked like they'd landed a world-beater when Hogh fired a hat-trick against Kilmarnock

As any striker going through a goalless run will attest, such matters start to consume you.

Hogh’s performances lately have become typical of so many in his position down the years. The touch is often cumbersome, the movement predictable, the predatory instincts dulled through a lack of confidence. It must feel like being in the darkest of tunnels.

The Dane’s current predicament is fascinating because he is not some journeyman who’s found a step up in class just too much for him.

A man with eight caps to his name, Celtic signed him for a record £11million in the summer because of his superb record at the highest level. Last year, in the colours of Bodo/Glimt, Hogh netted against Manchester City (twice), Atletico Madrid, Inter Milan and Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

The 25-year-old is – demonstrably – a player who is capable of delivering against any opponent.

The question is if he’s able to hit those heights in any jersey other than the one he vacated to move to Glasgow?

Hogh has scored goals against the likes of Manchester City, Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid

It’s not just its remote location above the Arctic Circle which makes Bodo/Glimt a curiosity in European football.

The vast majority of the players who move there or who come up through the academy feel right at home with the culture at the club which has been set by the impressive Kjetil Knutsen since 2018.

Bodo has its distinct way of doing things. And who’s to argue with the methodology? Under Knutsen and his sizeable entourage, it’s won four titles and the Norwegian Cup since 2020. Two seasons ago, it became the first Norwegian side to reach the semi-finals of a European competition.

There’s certainly something special about the environment which Knutsen has developed. The players who thrive there are all tailor-made for it. But whether they are all outstanding as individual footballers is a matter of some debate.

What’s notable in the Knutsen era is the number of players who Bodo/Glimt have sold who’ve looked like fish out of water elsewhere.

Victor Boniface, now of Bayer Leverkusen, had gone from strength to strength. Hugo Vetlesen has done well since moving to Club Brugge two years ago.

Celtic skipper Callum McGregor says it is up to the Celtic squad to help Hogh get back on track

But there’s a sizeable list of players who just haven’t cut it at other clubs. Patrick Berg, Fredrik Bjorkan and Jens Petter Hauge all departed the outpost with aspirations of cutting it in a bigger league only to return. Joel Mvuka, once of this parish, is now back at Bodo/Glimt after leaving Lorient.

Is it conceivable that Hogh is another of those who fitted into that unique club like a hand in a glove, but finds himself unable to replicate his form elsewhere? It’s beginning to look that way.

Right now, he appears ill-suited to whatever plan Celtic concoct while his scope for opportunities narrows.

This much can be safely said. With such a gargantuan price tag on his back and O’Neill duty-bound to select players he believes give him the best chance of winning matches, there’s no quick-fix solution to this.

#1663. Opinion: Liverpool now have to utilise 83-goal star after Arsenal defeat

Liverpool lost their second game of the season on the Sunday.

The Reds were facing Arsenal in a game which could have propelled them into the Premier League title race.

Instead, one mistake led to Mikel Arteta's men sitting back for most of the clash after they'd bagged their first goal.

Obviously, shutting up shop works for the Gunners but, it still feels like Liverpool should have done much better than they did.

They had barely any shots on target despite their attack being their most expensive ever.

Fans have been questioning whether Andoni Iraola is the right fit for Liverpool and now, questions are even being asked about some of his players with fans wanting the Spaniard to utilise every single option he has at his disposal.

Andoni Iraola confirms Liverpool should have done better with the chances that they had

Liverpool may have had four shots on target throughout their game against Arsenal on Sunday but, they didn't manage to convert any of them into goals.

Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak both kept coming up short which, for a duo who cost almost £250 million between them, is far from ideal.

This is why fans can't wait for Hugo Ekitike to return as, before he got injured last term, he was easily the Reds' best attacker and managed to convert almost every chance he was given.

But, now that he's not been available for a while, the cracks among Liverpool's attack are really starting to show.

In fact, after their defeat against Arsenal on Sunday, Iraola even said himself that his men should have done a lot better with the chances that they had.

"We had big chances. Cross bar, real big chances. We should have scored, and had enough to score today," he said in quotes relayed by Anfield Sector.

Federico Chiesa could help Liverpool convert their chances more often

Among their ranks, Liverpool have a fair few forgotten players.

However, none are as forgotten as Federico Chiesa. The Italian was brought in by Liverpool during Arne Slot's first season in charge with fans thinking that his £10 million fee was the bargain of the century.

But, after he returned from his ACL tear at Juventus, he was just never the same player which is why the Italian giants were probably so keen to get rid of him.

Now that he's back fit, fans thought Iraola would at least give him a chance to prove his worth but, he's not been given that privilege yet.

However, even though this hasn't happened yet, it doesn't mean that he still doesn't have stuff to offer Liverpool.

Throughout his career, he's bagged 83 goals and, the fact that he can play anywhere across the front three is another massive selling point.

Right now, Iraola is clearly trying to find his best front three so, even just giving Chiesa the chance to prove his worth could help him get closer to that.

Here's hoping that, before the January transfer window comes around, the Italian is given a chance.
