Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 19:08

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has suggested that Alejandro Balde still has a future at Camp Nou despite his struggles during the 2026-27 campaign.

Flick said ahead of Barcelona's clash with Alaves on Saturday that Balde currently does not have "the confidence he needs to play".

“Balde doesn’t have the confidence he needs to play, the conviction to attack and press high. The full-backs are very important for us, in our style of play. He needs confidence to reach his best level," Flick told reporters.

Balde was instead used off the bench, playing the final 28 minutes of the league fixture.

The Spain international has only played 116 minutes of action for Barcelona this season, and there is currently a host of speculation surrounding his future.

Manchester United are in the market for a left-back and could reignite their interest in the 23-year-old when the winter window opens for business.

Balde could potentially start Barcelona's Champions League fixture against Aston Villa on Tuesday, but it is more likely that he will again feature on the bench.

Flick has suggested that Balde is still in his plans moving forward, with the German determined to "help" the defender "regain his confidence".

“What’s happening to him is normal; when you don’t play often, you lack confidence. I see him training well, but we have to decide what’s best for the team, and Joao Cancelo is in great form,” Flick told reporters during his press conference.

“When I say he lacks confidence, I know it can affect him, and I spoke to him after the last press conference. I respect him a lot; he’s young, but he’s a great person and a very hard worker. I’ll help him regain his confidence.”

Balde has made 172 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions since breaking into their first team, scoring three goals and registering 21 assists.

Thierno Barry and his partner became the latest victims of footballer-targeted burglary on Thursday night while he was playing for Everton in their Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

Barry and his family are the latest victims in a string of footballer-targeted burglaries, with Morgan Gibbs-White's Nottinghamshire home raided just three days ago. Man United's Bruno Fernandes also had his Cheshire home burgled while he played in Como two weeks ago.

Barry's partner wrote: 'Unfortunately, our home was burgled this evening while we were at the football match.

'Thankfully, nobody was home at the time, but this is still an extremely distressing and violating experience for us and our family.

Thierno Barry and his partner Charlene appeared in a TikTok video on her profile recently dancing with different designer handbags in their walk-in wardrobe

The opportunistic thieves no doubt would have known Barry would not be at home, with his other half also out of the house watching him in action at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Last month, Charlene shared a video with her 20k TikTok followers inside the walk-in wardrobe in their house, dancing with designer handbags, which the burglars may have targeted during the break in.

Football stars have previously been warned about the dangers of sharing pictures or videos from within their luxury houses or alerting criminals to when they're out of the house on holiday.

A gang of burglars who targeted John Terry's house while he was away skiing in 2017 were jailed for a combined 28 years and the judge said: 'It might have been a mistake to post a family photograph on social media to show he was away on holiday.

'As a result his home was deliberately targeted and the master bedroom suite was ransacked.

Thieves took handbags worth £126,00, £220,000-worth of jewellery and signed first edition Harry Potter books worth £18,000.

Insurance companies have also warned against footballers sharing holiday snaps that may alert criminals of their absence.

Barry joins Gibbs-White as the second Premier League star burgled this week. The England international's partner Britney De Villiers, who lives with him and their two children, issued the statement on Instagram in an attempt to warn others to remain alert.

She wrote: 'I wasn’t going to publicly share this but our home was burgled a few days ago and after hearing about another one since, I feel it’s important to just warn others.

'It’s incredibly unsettling knowing that homes are being targeted. Please be extra vigilant, make sure your security systems are on whether you’re in the house or not and report anything suspicious.

United star Fernandes, wife Ana Pinho and their two young children were not at their luxury £4million property in Nether Alderley when three thieves struck at around 8.30pm on October 21 before making off with designer jewelry and other expensive items.

Barry scored for the Toffees in their 3-1 victory over Newcastle on Thursday night

Bruno Fernandes pictured at home with his wife Ana Pinho. The pair have two young children and were also victims of a burglary recently while he was away in Como

It’s understood that the house backs on to woods and the burglars jumped over the fence before breaking in, despite the Fernandes having installed CCTV and a high-tech alarm system.

Everton's neighbours Liverpool have had a number of players suffer the same experience over the years, with Sadio Mane, Dejan Lovren, Steven Gerrard, Dirk Kuyt, Pepe Reina, Robbie Keane and Lucas Leiva all going through the ordeal during their times at the club.

Peter Crouch and Abbey Clancy were victims on two separate occasions and a hooded gang raided Roberto Firmino's house in 2017. Thieves stole £70,000 worth of jewellery, watches and clothes on that occasion.

Another Everton player, Phil Jagielka, suffered a particularly harrowing episode in 2009 when he was held at knifepoint by an armed gang who broke into his house and forced him to open the safe.

Barry and his family are the latest victims of the highly upsetting targeting of footballers, with burglars fully aware of valuables kept on site.

Charlene appealed for any information that might lead to the burglars being caught

On Thursday evening before he heard the news of the break-in, Barry played the full 90 minutes for Everton and scored in the impressive victory.

Despite the win, much of the discussion on the night surrounded Jack Grealish's absence as he was dropped for failing to turn up to training.

But now the Manchester City loanee has been reprimanded for failing to show for Monday's work-out and was not part of the matchday squad on Thursday night.

Unusually, the club gave the reason in a statement on social media which accompanied the team news: 'Jarrad Branthwaite remains sidelined for a second successive game due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish is unavailable for selection due to a breach of Club discipline.'

#1589. Barcelona, Lille and Brighton and Hove Albion scout Estoril teenager Jordan Arnolin

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 19:19, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 19:19

Barcelona are reportedly taking a close interest in Jordan Arnolin, but the Estoril centre-back is also attracting attention in France and the Premier League.

Barcelona are not only looking to sign established players to strengthen their defence. The Catalan club, leader in LaLiga, are also scouting young European talents, and according to Portuguese newspaper Record, they sent a representative to the Estadio do Dragao on Saturday to watch 18-year-old Arnolin.

The interest comes as Barcelona have spent several months trying to strengthen their back line. The sporting department is working on several profiles, with the aim of finding a centre-back who can give Hansi Flick more guarantees.

The name of Inter Milan stalwart Alessandro Bastoni has been mentioned insistently in recent months, most recently by Sky Sports. The Italy international would be an especially expensive operation, however, and Inter have no reason to make his departure easy. Against that backdrop, a young player with high potential is another route for the Barcelona hierarchy, and Arnolin fits that logic.

Barcelona will have to contend with two other suitors. According to Record, Lille and Brighton and Hove Albion also sent representatives to the Dragao to monitor the young Portuguese.

For Lille, the move would fit a well-established recruitment policy of backing high-potential players who can take a step up and increase in value. The northern French club have regularly used that model to bring in players who are not yet well known to the wider public. Brighton are a far stronger financial rival, with greater resources than Lille and their own reputation for finding talent. Their ability to attract young players and offer them exposure in the Premier League is another argument in their favour.

Lille face a stiff challenge. Barcelona have a sporting and media pull that is unmatched, and even though Arnolin would probably not walk straight into Flick’s starting line-up, joining the Catalan club would be hard for an 18-year-old to turn down.

Lille do have one strong argument in playing time. With heavy competition in the Barcelona squad, particularly at centre-back, the young Portuguese could have to wait for first-team chances, while a gradual path to the Lille first team looks easier to envisage.

The financial side remains a factor, too. Brighton have more room for manoeuvre, and Barcelona keep considerable economic strength and international appeal, despite their well-known budget constraints. Lille will probably have to rely on their sporting project and their ability to support the defender’s progress.

Another element could complicate negotiations. Arnolin has just signed his first professional contract with Estoril, running until June 2029, so the club are under no pressure to sell. Lille have a card to play, but they will need to be convincing to beat two very serious competitors.

#1587. BRYAN ROBSON: Stretford End's 'standards' banner made me sad - I never needed reminding of them. It's not about you, it's about hard work and Man United winning... I would never have called out Sir Alex Ferguson in public

Published: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026

Standards. The demand has always been to keep them high at Manchester United; you were aware the minute you walked through the door.

I'd like to think I never needed reminding of them by the Stretford End at least. Ron Atkinson, my manager, made me aware but I knew myself what was expected.

This was a club that had won the biggest trophies with Sir Matt Busby and Sir Bobby Charlton, great football names renowned throughout the world. I got to know both, as well as other greats, George Best and Denis Law.

You knew you were striving for excellence, to win, to be the best but when I met Sir Matt and Sir Bob, their fundamental message was ‘work hard’. Work hard, pull no punches in training, train as you mean to play and the enjoyment, the success, will come.

Sir Matt had been a miner as well as a player. He was an army man in the war, a company sergeant major, so that military influence, the work ethic, that discipline on the training ground, was born out of that.

It was instilled in you at United. He wanted his players to carry that forward. Yes, entertain but you must work hard, then you will have pride in what you represent.

I'd like to think I never needed reminding of Manchester United's standards. Work hard, pull no punches in training, train as you mean to play and the enjoyment, the success, will come

When Sir Alex Ferguson (left) came into the club, he had the standards already ingrained in him - and took United back to the top as Sir Matt Busby (right) had before him

Sir Matt (second left) and Sir Bobby Charlton (right, pictured celebrating winning the European Cup in 1968) gave the United players that followed them a fundamental message: ‘Work hard’

When Sir Alex Ferguson came into the club, he had that already ingrained in him. When we won the Cup Winners’ Cup in 1991 then the league title in 1993, I'll never forget the smile on Sir Matt's face; the realisation we were back at the top. It is what he had always dreamed of.

He and Sir Bob loved talking about how important it was to do well both domestically and in Europe. Perpetuating that legacy of the Busby Babes: ‘Remember who you are representing.’ Dress smartly, a good haircut, club tie, club blazer. No earrings, no ponytails. Standards.

So when you see the Stretford End unfurl a banner, reminding players today what they believe is missing, it’s sad to see. That my face adorns that banner, alongside Roy Keane and Eric Cantona, I’m thankful. Thankful that I’m appreciated because I always set out to give the fans everything and because Roy and Eric carried on the same work I put in with them as captain.

United’s players today must give full commitment to the club, those fans and ultimately, themselves. Representing Manchester United with all its history is a privileged role, the responsibility never weighed heavy on me, I always enjoyed it and today’s players should equally embrace the challenge.

I was fortunate to have good tutors in my younger days at West Brom. Hardened professionals such as John Wile, Tony Brown, Len Cantello and Asa Hartford. I saw the value of how they fostered team spirit, building friendships on trips to Worcester races, going for dinner together and playing charity golf or cricket tournaments.

You got to understand your team-mates better. You realised what was going on at home may be affecting how they were at training. Who could take a telling off, who needed an arm round the shoulder. It brought you closer and you looked after each other, on and off the pitch.

When I was made captain at United, I took those practices with me. Importantly, we always stuck together. If I were in the United dressing room now, I’d be saying, first and foremost, statistics tell us work rate must change. Step it up. Secondly, stick together.

Nothing should be coming out on social media or television, certainly not criticism of the staff. Those players know who they are. What needs to be said stays in the dressing room. If you need to have a fight, have the fight but it stays in-house.

The Stretford End unfurled a banner with my face alongside Roy Keane and Eric Cantona last weekend. The message was clear

Representing Manchester United with all its history is a privileged role, the responsibility never weighed heavy on me, I always enjoyed it and today’s players should embrace the challenge

Nothing should be coming out on social media or television, certainly not criticism of the staff as has happened recently with Bruno Fernandes attacking Michael Carrick (left)

I saw many a fight in the dressing room but it wasn’t for the public’s benefit. And I certainly wouldn’t challenge the manager in public. I had no problem saying I disagreed with Sir Alex to his face, but behind closed doors. You can't agree all the time, that's life, but the only way you progress is to stay together.

On the pitch, predominantly, you adhere to the tactics you've been given but if you're losing control of a game then work it out yourselves. For example, if Steve Bruce and Gary Pallister were getting overloaded, I'd sometimes ask Brian McClair to drop back into midfield to pick up my man so I could drop deeper and help the defence. When I got back into the dressing room the gaffer would either say 'great, now reorganise' or I'd get the hairdryer! But that was why you were captain, to take responsibility.

I always wanted to set an example by how I played but it’s not always possible to play well and it was important, because of that team bond we built, that the other lads were equally confident in giving me a rollicking if I needed it too.

It doesn't matter who you are, it's not about you, it's about Manchester United winning. Michael Carrick doesn't need players throwing their arms in the air, he needs them to knuckle down.

Michael invited me in to Carrington a few times earlier in the year and the training and attitude looked good. It got results. They know what's required. As Sir Matt said, hard work is the base for any improvement.

#1586. Ezri Konsa, the best Arsenal signing of last window, gives Mikel Arteta a welcome selection headache

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 19:29

Arsenal’s outstanding defensive display in the 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday ended a 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at their rival’s ground. The result was built on superb organisation and discipline in front of David Raya’s goal, and one of the standout names was Ezri Konsa.

The England defender produced a top-level performance to secure the clean sheet. According to Opta, he won eight of nine duels, made eight clearances, five tackles, five recoveries and two blocks, and won two fouls.

For the first time in the Premier League era, Liverpool did not register a single shot on target in a game at Anfield, a mark that highlights the outstanding collective defending and the performance of the centre-back pairing. Konsa’s understanding with Gabriel Magalhaes makes it look as though the two have played together for many seasons.

So far, Konsa has maintained the high level he showed at his former club, Aston Villa. He has made only 13 appearances for the Gunners this season, yet he already merits the label of a successful signing. His assured displays have almost made supporters forget who held the position before his arrival.

The 29-year-old joined Arsenal in August for £51m to replace William Saliba, who suffered a serious back injury that forced him off in the World Cup semi-final between France and Spain.

Saliba, who is not expected to return until the end of this month, had been one of Arsenal’s defensive foundations in recent seasons, and the club decided to bring in an outside name, even though Christian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie, Riccardo Calafiori and Jurrien Timber could all have played there.

From here, boss Mikel Arteta will have the kind of selection headache every manager dreams of. Konsa and Saliba will compete at a high level to play alongside Gabriel Magalhaes, and Arsenal can only benefit.

The season is long and the Gunners will compete for every trophy. Having elite players both on the pitch and on the bench is essential to withstand the physical strain over the months ahead.

In recent seasons, Arsenal have made good signings, especially in defence, such as Timber, Calafiori and Hincapie. Konsa shares a key characteristic with those names. His versatility, as he can also play at right-back, gives Arteta a range of options very few European clubs can match, and over a long season that could prove decisive.

“Then there’s the transfer market. Milan wants to present themselves with confidence. The defender they didn’t sign in the summer could arrive in January. I mentioned Gonçalo Inacio’s name last week and I’ll continue to mention it.

“He remains a highly sought-after player. There are other options, but the defender is a key issue for Milan. It won’t end here. I expect a move in attack, and Milan will certainly do something other than the defender.”

#1583. Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they currently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

We will be getting team news shortly and will be bringing you the pre-match updates as they come.

#1582. Boga’s limited minutes put focus on Zhegrova before Lazio

Luciano Spalletti outlined different considerations for Jérémie Boga and Edon Zhegrova before Juventus faced Lazio: Boga was fit for around half an hour, while Zhegrova’s performances had earned him a case for more playing time. His remarks, reported by Pazzi di Fanta and echoed in Juventus’ official press-conference account, point to contrasting immediate options rather than a settled hierarchy.

The distinction is grounded in what Spalletti said about their readiness and impact, not in an announced tactical role for either player. Boga remained available, but with his minutes limited; Zhegrova had impressed the coach with qualities and unpredictable play. Juventus’ official account also said the winger could start against Lazio.

For Boga, the clearest point was physical: Spalletti said he had about 30 minutes in his legs. That makes him an option for a defined contribution, rather than a player the coach said was ready to last a full match. It does not mean Boga was unavailable or ruled out of the selection.

Zhegrova’s case was different. Spalletti praised the qualities he had shown and said his performances warranted more playing time. The official Juventus account added that his unpredictable play could surprise opponents, while also reporting that he could start against Lazio.

That contrast suggests Zhegrova offered a possible route to changing the match through his attacking unpredictability, whereas Boga’s immediate involvement was constrained by fitness. It is an interpretation of Spalletti’s comments, not confirmation that the coach assigned them fixed or mutually exclusive positions. The pair’s different recent contributions have also featured in Juventus coverage of Zhegrova’s attacking impact.

Spalletti’s comments on team balance add an important qualification. The official account said the coach was weighing how to fit several attacking players into the side, taking both the opponent and the team’s overall balance into consideration. Praise for Zhegrova did not, by itself, guarantee a starting place.

The coach also rejected a rigid division between starters and substitutes, saying Juventus needed to widen the group of players considered starters. He was still assessing his selection and how the game might develop, with the possibility that starting certain attackers together would leave fewer options to influence the match later.

That broader approach prevents a simple reading in which Boga becomes a permanent bench option and Zhegrova takes over a defined role. Spalletti’s remarks were about the choices available for this fixture: Boga could contribute for roughly half an hour, while Zhegrova’s performances had strengthened his claim to more minutes. Neither statement settles their status over the season.

There is also a difference between being praised and being selected. Spalletti’s assessment gave Zhegrova positive momentum, and Juventus’ account explicitly left open a start against Lazio, but the coach said the final decision still depended on balance and the opposition. Boga, meanwhile, remained available within the fitness limit Spalletti had described.

The immediate comparison is therefore one of management: Boga’s involvement had a stated physical ceiling, while Zhegrova’s was supported by the coach’s view of his performances and unpredictability. That points to different ways they might help Juventus, without establishing a permanent tactical distinction. Boga’s recent place in the side has also been discussed alongside his selection in an attacking role.

Spalletti’s comments leave the practical question to the team selection and the match itself. Juventus’ official account said Zhegrova could start; Boga was available for around 30 minutes. Those were the clearest parameters ahead of Lazio, with no fixed pecking order announced.

Federica Mancuso has followed Juventus through every high and low she can remember, growing up in Turin where the club was never just a team but a way of life. Her writing focuses on what actually happens on the pitch, breaking down formations, pressing structures, and the tactical decisions that often go unnoticed in match coverage. She believes understanding how Juventus play is just as important as knowing the scoreline.

#1580. Inside Marc Guehi's 'complicated' month - and why Enzo Maresca won't drop his Man City 'lieutenant' despite errors for club and country

Published: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 08:09 EDT, 30 October 2026

Manchester City’s famous five were all afforded holidays at the start of this week and there must have been some discussion about making that number half a dozen instead.

The quintet were all on the touchline during the warm-ups before City progressed through to the quarter-finals of another Carabao Cup defence on Wednesday night. With Erling Haaland’s oversized wool coat and Ruben Dias in leathers with a cap on backwards, it could’ve been mistaken for fashion week.

Enzo Maresca’s decision to grant three days off after defeat by Aston Villa was made with mental and physical fatigue in mind. The five, also including Gianluigi Donnarumma, Elliot Anderson and Josko Gvardiol, had all played over 850 minutes each so far this season.

But so too had Marc Guehi. And yet as those not required took their seats behind the dugout, he was straightening the captain’s armband and cajoling a group who traded blows with Brighton and then squeezed through on penalties.

Another full match to his name, the centre-half jogging 30 yards from the centre circle to console Mateo Kovacic after the Croatian’s miss in the shootout.

‘After two complicated games, I think he was very good,’ Maresca said of the only member of his leadership group called to participate in midweek.

While the rest of the Manchester City leadership group sat out Wednesday night's victory over Brighton in the Carabao Cup, Marc Guehi was captain and played the full 90 minutes

Rayan Cherki, Guehi and Enzo Fernandez celebrate the penalty shootout win over Brighton

Guehi was at the World Cup longer than Haaland, Dias and Gvardiol. He also featured in 332 of the 360 minutes comprising England’s four-game international window last month and will surely earn a rest at some point soon. Not that he thinks he needs one.

Maresca clearly felt there were compelling reasons for keeping Guehi going. If it was a straight decision between him or Dias for Brighton – with one needing to shepherd the back line against dangerous opposition – then the Portuguese’s extra game-and-a-half worth of minutes probably contributed. Guehi is younger and can likely bounce back quicker.

And then there is the recent form, some high-profile slips, and the manager’s psychology around that. Guehi admitted fault for both Ipswich Town goals in a 3-2 victory – caught the wrong side on both occasions – and then miscontrolled a Dias pass in the opening moments at Villa, allowing Nicolas Jackson to open the scoring.

Maresca hooked a booked Guehi at half-time in the Midlands, something ex-City defender Joleon Lescott feared could ‘shatter’ the defender’s confidence when discussing it on television. These mistakes came after Lamine Yamal had picked his pocket in the Nations League defeat by Spain at Wembley last month.

City’s manager has been defiant about Guehi this week. Aside from the praise after Brighton, he has talked up the 26-year-old’s ability to compartmentalise and react to setbacks.

Guehi is good at holding his hands up to team-mates and taking ownership, not hiding in the dressing room. It was one of the reasons why Maresca – who felt he needed an Englishman among his captains – chose Guehi as a lieutenant for first-choice skipper Dias. ‘I love Marc to be honest,’ the City boss said, somebody he chose to feature in central midfield on the opening weekend of the season.

There is definitely a school of thought around City that Guehi is best playing his way back into proper form, that Brighton provided a decent opportunity for that. His overall performances this season have been an improvement on his first six months at the Etihad Stadium, an imperious display at Old Trafford when the team were a man light his finest to date.

That followed a similarly impressive night in Porto, while he was the only defender to come out with real credit from the manic 5-3 win over Sunderland. Those were before the independent commission’s findings of City’s guilt for systematic breaking of financial rules, with England manager Thomas Tuchel revealing that the City players in his squad were naturally worried about the immediate future.

Ruben Dias has a word with Guehi after the Englishman's mistake led to Aston Villa taking the lead at Villa Park last weekend

Guehi had his pocket picked by goalscorer Lamine Yamal in England's loss to Spain in September

Concerns were allayed during meetings with chief executive Ferran Soriano and Maresca, with Guehi later stressing his ‘trust’ in the club’s insistence of their innocence.

This has been a whirlwind year, Guehi's move to Liverpool collapsing last summer as he lay inside the MRI scanner during a medical and then City accelerating interest in January to give them a defensive boost amid an injury crisis.

Guehi has barely had time to stand still, wrapping his head around the unique demands of working with Pep Guardiola after being so settled at Crystal Palace and then meeting another new manager within months.

Maresca has brought a slightly new way of defending, a more aggressive press – with even Dias storming into midfield at Villa on Saturday – and that has left more gaps to contend with at the back. It’s high risk and the likes of Guehi have to remain hyper-vigilant. It will likely take time for them all to settle into this.

#1578. Spalletti identifies Juventus changes after 3-0 Lazio loss

Luciano Spalletti said Juventus were inferior to Lazio after their 3-0 home defeat on Sunday, 18 October, admitting the performance had surprised him. The assessment, reported by Football Italia, came just days after the Bianconeri had beaten Celta Vigo in the Europa League.

Juventus rarely threatened to recover in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard headed Lazio ahead, Gustav Isaksen added a second with an angled finish and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru sealed the result on a late counter-attack. Spalletti said his side had returned from Vigo at 4am on Friday after their 2-1 comeback win, then had time to recover with the performance staff.

He had made six changes, but felt Juventus were slow in both body and thought. His criticism covered the lack of tempo, ideas, running and willingness to work, as well as the team’s weakness in duels and its response when things went wrong. Those concerns followed a previous Juventus defeat that had also prompted scrutiny of the team’s competitive response.

Spalletti was absent from the touchline because of a ban following his altercation with Cagliari’s Fabio Pisacane; assistant Marco Domenichini deputised. Juventus have 11 points after seven league rounds, eight behind the leaders. Football Italia noted that Igor Tudor’s team had one more point at the same stage last season, while Thiago Motta’s side had collected 13.

Supporters who stayed until the final whistle jeered and insulted the squad. Spalletti said the response now had to come on the pitch, rather than the players giving in to events, and identified two areas for review: how he communicates with the team and the working method. He said he needed to examine his relationship with the players and decide what must change.

Speaking to DAZN Italia after the match, Spalletti said Juventus had neither controlled the game nor shown a clear idea of how to shape it. He considered the performance unacceptable and said he would reflect carefully on it. His next task is to determine whether the adjustment lies in his approach to the group, the work itself, or both.

#1575. How 'football geek' Kim Hellberg turned Middlesbrough into the 'PSG of the Championship' - thanks to 'Del Boy and Rodney', the next Harry Kane and the transfer strategy that's taken them to a new level

Published: 13:14 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 08:53 EDT, 30 October 2026

I was sat in the press conference room at St Mary’s Stadium back in May when Kim Hellberg forced back tears as he talked about everything he’d sacrificed. All the time spent away from his family, all those nights when he called them to say he wouldn’t be coming home because he had more Southampton matches to watch.

And despite them all, there the Middlesbrough manager still sat, beaten in the second leg of the Championship play-off semi-final by a manager who sent staff to spy on his training session and who was, for now, going to Wembley.

‘I have nothing to say to him,’ Hellberg had replied when asked if he had spoken to Southampton boss Tonda Eckert. Hellberg had already completed his TV and local radio interviews but informed club staff that he still had things, about sacrifices, that he wanted to say.

In the end, of course, it was not over for Hellberg and Boro. Thanks to Daily Mail Sport’s stunning Spygate exclusive, Saints were eventually expelled and Boro went to Wembley in their place. By then, though, the chaos had taken its toll. Those who saw Hellberg in the build-up to the play-off final described him as exhausted and drained.

As did his players, who were left in limbo as they tried, somehow, to remain fit and alert. Luke Ayling, the club’s captain, found out they were going to Wembley while he was bathing his young son just days before the final. Middlesbrough lost to Hull, and had to prepare for a 10th successive season in the Championship. They should have gone up automatically but blew it, having spent most of the season second in the table.

All of that madness and heartbreak could, quite easily, have left Boro with too many scars and yet they host Charlton this weekend sitting top of the Championship, on a 10-game unbeaten run. Somehow, Boro have kicked on again and sources close to the dressing room believe they are better set than ever for a return to the top flight.

Kim Hellberg has led Middlesbrough to the top of the Championship as they banish all memories of Spygate

Aidan Morris celebrates scoring against Burnley last month - Boro are flying as they welcome Charlton on Saturday on a 10-game unbeaten run

For a start, Spygate has barely been mentioned. There’s been no talk of it, according to club insiders, except to discuss the impending return to St Mary’s at the end of November, one which everyone expects to be poisonous.

That has certainly not been helped by the FA’s decision to, effectively, let Eckert off scot free, and how much the Saints and their fans have appeared to revel in it. ‘Everyone in football knows it’s nonsense,’ said one source.

Boro, meanwhile, have just got better. It helps when you play like Paris Saint-Germain. ‘People might laugh,’ said Hellberg, who twice made a point last week of claiming Boro’s style of play shows similarities to the French giants. Hellberg watched PSG’s clash with Barcelona in the Champions League and was drawn to the similar ‘massive spaces’ left in their midfield as they look to be brave in attack.

That is how Hellberg wants his side to play, as risky as it sometimes looks to the casual observer, because it means creating a horde of good chances. They have the most xG (expected goals, which measures the quality of chances created) of any team in the league. Their 'expected goal difference', the gulf between the chances they create and concede, has rocketed since Hellberg took over from Rob Edwards almost a year ago.

Now, they have the player they needed to take those chances in striker Will Lankshear, the Championship’s top scorer, who has recently been labelled the ‘next Harry Kane’. No pressure.

Having been released by Arsenal, then gone through the Tottenham academy (via Sheffield United) before being sent out on loan to several clubs, there are plenty of parallels there, not least because Lankshear is proving himself to be one of the most lethal English strikers around.

His 11 goals so far in the Championship make him the leading scorer across the top four divisions of English football, with two more than Erling Haaland. Like Kane, he’s a superb technical finisher.

There was some surprise when Tottenham agreed to sell him in the summer for an initial £8million that could rise to £20m. But with Roberto De Zerbi showing little interest in academy players, Lankshear knew he had to make a move to get game time. Spurs inserted a matching rights clause should anyone try to swoop in for him.

Will Lankshear's 11 goals so far in the Championship make him the leading scorer across the top four divisions of English football, with two more than Erling Haaland

Sources close to the dressing room talk of a thoughtful, intelligent lad – ‘his head’s screwed on right,’ says one – who left money on the table to join Boro despite more lucrative offers from elsewhere in the Championship, Europe, and Premier League, including Leeds, because he knew he would be given the minutes to flourish, in a team that creates heaps of chances and just needed someone to finish them off.

‘I’ve learnt as much as I have my whole life in one week under Kim,’ said Lankshear recently.

So much of Boro’s hopes, say insiders, rest on Lankshear’s shoulders. Hellberg rested him for their recent game against Cardiff, only for the 21-year-old to come off the bench to score the equaliser. You suspect he won’t be making the same mistake again.

Sources describe Hellberg as a ‘football geek’. He grew up, like many men in their 30s, playing Football Manager. When previewing Boro’s trip to Bolton last week, a thumping 5-1 win that sent them top, Hellberg said he hadn’t been there before but remembered playing against the likes of Jay-Jay Okocha and Kevin Nolan on the video game. One of his heroes, Frank Lampard, phoned him to offer some words of advice ahead of the play-off final.

Hellberg celebrated the Bolton win by rewatching the game three times. He’d likely have watched it more if they lost.

When he was asked by a Charlton reporter last season if he had ever been to the Valley, Hellberg revealed he had with his dad Stefan, also a football coach in Sweden, during tours of a few grounds in London when he was a young boy.

Hellberg is described as a hands-on coach, one who likes to bombard his players with video clips about the minutiae of their game, and their opponents'. He’s hot on his data. Those who see him week in, week out, say he’s forever dropping stats into conversations and press conferences.

His first role was in the part-time Swedish seventh tier, during which he worked as a gymnastics teacher, and in a kindergarten teaching three to six-year-olds. ‘They are more like the players than you think,’ said Hellberg.

Sources talk of Lankshear as a thoughtful, intelligent lad – ‘his head’s screwed on right,’ says one – who left money on the table to join Boro despite more lucrative offers

So much of Boro’s hopes, say insiders, rest on Lankshear’s shoulders

As with many clubs on the rise – and on the slide – the foundations for that success, or failure, come from far above the grass. Just days after the Wembley heartache, Hellberg sat down with head of football Kieran Scott and head of recruitment Chris Jones to draw up their plans and key targets for the summer. Boro landed most of them.

They beat lots of clubs to Lankshear, whom they had tracked for a while. They snapped up Ashley Phillips, also from Spurs, who was their top defensive target. And Radek Vitek, from Manchester United, their top goalkeeper target.

The loan arrival of Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry was described as the ‘icing on the cake’. Adilson Malanda, the French centre back, was described by one source as the ‘nearest we’ve had to Jonathan Woodgate since Jonathan Woodgate’.

‘We signed the quality that we didn’t have 12 months ago,’ said one club insider. ‘They are a level better. That’s the huge difference.’ This is what Boro have got really good at. Signing players to improve them, develop them, and sell them on at a huge profit.

Scott and Jones, who describe themselves as ‘Del Boy and Rodney’ due to their constant need to sell the club to potential signings who might have glitzier offers, don’t have hordes of analysts but sit there themselves with data software SkillCorner and StatsBomb. And it’s working.

A report by the CIES Football Observatory showed that Boro’s players have appreciated in value by nearly £150m over the last five years – the ninth-highest total in the country, ahead of Villa and Arsenal and just behind Chelsea.

They consistently make a profit on their stars. They signed Morgan Rogers for £1m in 2023 only to sell him to Villa for up to £17m seven months later. When he joined Chelsea this summer for £117m, they banked another £21m as a world-record sell-on fee.

Finn Azaz signed for £2m and was sold to Saints for £12m. Emmanuel Latte Lath, signed for £5m and flogged for £22.5m. Rav van den Berg, signed for less than £500k and sold for £11m.

The loan arrival of Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry was described as the ‘icing on the cake’

Morgan Rogers (centre) was bought for £2m, sold for £17m seven months later and earned Boro another £21m in sell-on fees when he moved to Chelsea this summer

‘There is something special happening around this place,’ said one source. ‘On the field, off the field, recruitment. Everything is coming together’

Academy players have brought in huge profits, too. Like Hayden Hackney, who joined Everton in the summer for £16.5m, Djed Spence, who headed for Spurs in a move worth up to £20m and Marcus Tavernier, who signed for Bournemouth for £12m. As Del Boy would say, lovely jubbly.

The last time Boro lost in the play-off final, to Norwich in 2015, chairman and owner Steve Gibson gave a rousing speech to his troops to promise they would come back stronger, and they did. They went up automatically the following season. There is a similar feeling now around Teesside.

Club insiders talk of the strongest bond between the club and the community since the days of Juninho and Fabrizio Ravanelli in the 90s. Their attendances, in what is the year of their 150th anniversary, are their highest since they were last in the Premier League.

‘There is something special happening around this place,’ said one source. ‘On the field, off the field, recruitment. Everything is coming together.’

Mikel Arteta will inevitably be quizzed for an update on Saliba in his pre-game press conference if he does appear, but the Spaniard is likely to keep his cards close to his chest.

However, the 25-year-old may be in with a slim chance of making the squad against Hull City this weekend, or Arsenal's first game back following the international break away to Newcastle United on November 21.

Saliba made 50 appearances for Arsenal across all competitions in the 2025-26 season, including 30 Premier League starts and 12 in the Champions League, while playing 4,254 minutes in total.

The former Saint-Etienne starlet also started six games for France at the 2026 World Cup, but he was taken off in the 30th minute of Les Bleus' semi-final loss to Spain as a result of his back problem.

Saliba's imminent return to first-team football will give Arteta the best selection dilemma imaginable, thanks to Ezri Konsa's seamless integration into the Arsenal backline.

The England international has already played his part in five clean sheets in the 2026-27 Premier League season and produced another defensive masterclass in Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool, as his relationship with Gabriel Magalhaes blossoms further.

Konsa should expect to maintain his undisputed starter status for the next few weeks at least, while Saliba builds his match fitness back up, and the 29-year-old can be viewed as a genuine competitor to the Frenchman, not just his backup.

However, if Saliba can return to the level he was performing at in each of the past four years, expect the 25-year-old to eventually regain his rightful spot in the Arsenal back four, even if Konsa has been one of the signings of the season so far.
