#1541. Hearts' Riccarton Three - 20 years on: The dressing-room rebellion that pulled back the curtain on the madness of Vladimir Romanov's Tynecastle reign and altered the club's trajectory for generations to come

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:23 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 13:51 EDT, 30 October 2026

Only those individuals who’d been living in a cave for a year or so would have believed that all was well in Hearts’ world when they recorded a storied triumph over Hibs at Hampden 20 years ago.

A thumping four-nil win in the Scottish Cup semi-final on April 2, 2006, came courtesy of Paul Hartley’s hat-trick with Edgaras Jankauskas also getting in on the act.

As if there wasn’t enough for the maroon hordes to gloat about that afternoon, Ivan Sproule and Gary Smith were sent off for Tony Mowbray’s team.

With lower-league Gretna awaiting Hearts in the final, it should have felt like the good times were rolling. And, to an extent, they were.

The following month, the Gorgie men would beat Aberdeen to wrap up second place in the top flight and earn a place in the Champions League qualifiers.

With Gretna beaten on penalties ten days later, an open-top bus wove its way through the streets of the capital with the old trophy being shown off.

Paul Hartley, Steven Pressley and Craig Gordon hit out at the club's ownership in October 2006

Only six months earlier, Hearts had thumped rivals Hibs in the Scottish Cup semi-final

But the jubilant scenes were a distortion of the real picture. Vladimir Romanov, the Russian-Lithuanian business leader, had bought into the club in February 2005, becoming the majority shareholder eight months later.

He promised lavish investment to establish Hearts not only as the dominant club in Scotland, but as a European force to be reckoned with. Many supporters wearing Cossack hats lapped it up and were disinclined to look beyond the bluff and the bluster — or examine the price tag.

Those with a stronger grasp of the situation saw Romanov for what he was: An erratic egomaniac who’d be ruinous for the club in the longer term. The only question was how quickly it would take for it all to come crashing down.

It hardly required inside knowledge to appreciate that his eccentricities were going to test the patience of Hearts supporters from the get-go.

Despite the side sitting on top of the league after winning their first eight games of the 2005-06 season, Romanov sacked manager George Burley with chief executive Phil Anderton also fired.

Graham Rix, a convicted sex offender, was hired as Burley’s replacement before Valdas Ivanauskas was brought in on an interim basis in March 2006.

The former FBK Kaunas coach was given the full-time gig after winning the cup only to be put on sick leave with stress at the start of the following season.

Ivanauskas’ temporary replacement, Eduard Malofeev, the sporting director, barely spoke a word of English.

The preposterous turnover of managers was just the tip of the iceberg, though.

Rumours abounded that Romanov was in charge of team selection and would often fax in his line-up before kick-off — a matter Rix subsequently confirmed as being true. Players who were fit were routinely shunted to the sidelines for no reason.

At the owner’s behest, a mysterious woman from Eastern Europe joined the physio department. Brandishing a divination stick, she claimed to be able to identify injuries before they happened.

Accustomed to training in mornings throughout their careers, players were told to report for work in evenings — with no explanation. One recalled a session in the dark winding down with a wheelbarrow race.

For many, the final straw arrived when Romanov started to deliver his own motivational team talks.

It may have had the veneer of a professional football club, but it was a circus.

‘The place was an absolute shambles,’ said defender and future Hearts manager Robbie Neilson.

Behind the scenes, the senior players spoke privately about their deepening concerns and contemplated going public with them.

After weeks of procrastinating, they agreed that doing nothing was no longer an option. And so, on October 27, 2006 — just six months after that routing of Hibs — ‘The Riccarton Three’ were born.

Vladimir Romanov promised  Hearts fans that the club would dominate Scottish football

Hearts had lost at home to Kilmarnock the previous Saturday and were scheduled to play Dunfermline at Tynecastle the following day.

The press pack which descended on the training ground inside Heriot-Watt University was larger than normal on that cold morning for a reason. They’d been tipped off that something remarkable would unfold. ‘Bring your popcorn,’ wrote a message from one of the squad.

With Malofeev elsewhere in the building and the rest of the squad sitting in a dressing room, at 12.02pm the doors to the seminar room opened and the show began.

In walked Hartley and Craig Gordon, stony-faced. Between them, beanie hat on his head and holding a piece of paper, was captain Steven Pressley.

By the time the trio took their place at a table filled with microphones, it was clear that the next few minutes were going to blow the doors off the club. This was a dressing room revolution.

‘It was the crossing of the Rubicon,’ said Neilson. ‘As soon as you did that there was no way back.’

Despite knowing that he was unleashing a verbal grenade, Pressley delivered the words with complete calmness.

‘Chaps, just to make you aware that I’m going to make a statement and we’ll answer no questions,’ he said.

‘This is a statement on behalf of a number of the players.

‘I have tried along with the coaching staff and certain colleagues to implement the correct values and disciplines, but it has become an impossible task.

‘There is only so much a coaching staff, a captain, and certain colleagues can do without the full backing, direction, and coherence of the manager and those running the football club.

‘While, publicly, I have expressed the need for unity behind the scenes, I have made my concerns abundantly clear.

‘The last two years have been very testing for the players. Together, we have faced a number of challenges and worked hard at retaining some degree of unity.

George Burley was sacked by Romanov despite winning his first eight top-flight fixtures

‘However, due to the circumstances, morale, understandably, is not good and there is significant unrest within the dressing room.’

Pressley didn’t mention Romanov by name but he didn’t have to. Hartley and Gordon remained silent throughout the address.

And with that, they rose and left, the hush in the room in sharp contrast with the chatter of a normal post-match conference.

Although even the most experienced journalists present were stunned at what they’d witnessed, they knew this much: Nothing would ever be the same again.

Predictably, the fallout was nuclear. Seething with what he saw on Sky Sports bulletins elsewhere in the building, Romanov addressed the entire squad and told them they’d be sold if they didn’t beat Dunfermline. The game ended 1-1.

The three actually started the match. Malofeev gave a strange post-match interview where he angrily insisted there were no problems at the club and the players could say what they liked because it was a ‘democracy’.

A short time later, the actions of Romanov would prove this was not the case.

Pressley was dropped for the game against Falkirk on November 13, was an unused substitute against Rangers on November 19, was then stripped of the captaincy and left the club on December 9 ahead of a January switch to Celtic.

Bizarrely, on the day he was told he’d no future at Hearts, he was offered the assistant manager’s job.

‘I was probably seen as the figurehead of the club at the time,’ he later said. ‘Everybody leaned on me to try and get things done, or get answers within the club.

‘The treatment of some individuals was horrendous. The honesty, the transparency, all the things that I think are really important in the foundations of a club — they were being disregarded.’

Hartley was a substitute against Falkirk and also moved to Parkhead in the January for £1.1million.

Gordon, the most valuable asset, was dropped for away games with Dundee United and Rangers, but remained at the club until he joined Sunderland for £9m in the summer.

As for Malofeev? Hearts didn’t win a game under him. He stayed in charge until Ivanauskas resumed his duties in late November.

With Hearts knocked out of the Scottish Cup by Dunfermline in the New Year, a game in which Gordon was a substitute, Ivanauskas then made way for Anatoliy Korobochka, the latest director of football to be promoted to head coach.

Despite an upturn in results, Aberdeen claimed third place ahead of the Tynecastle side. So much for winning the title.

While the Riccarton Three were never going to topple Romanov purely by speaking out against him, their actions ensured he was never viewed in the same light again by supporters.

Eduard Malofeev failed to win a single match during his short spell in the Tynecastle dugout

When Stephen Frail was made manager in January 2008, he was able to demand that he would have full responsibility for team selection.

By the following year, Romanov had ceded the day-to-day running to Campbell Ogilvie. His visits to Tynecastle became increasingly less frequent.

No doubt, this had much to do with what he knew was coming down the track.

Although Hearts did defeat Hibs 5-1 in the 2012 Scottish Cup Final, the recklessness of the Romanov years was catching up with the club.

The following year, the collapse of his Lithuania-based Ukio Bankas triggered Hearts calling in the administrators who uncovered debts of £15m. A 15-point deduction and relegation followed.

Were it not for the mobilisation of the Foundation of Hearts and the largesse of Ann Budge, one of Scotland’s great sporting institutions would have gone under.

From the rubble, the club was rebuilt. With Tony Bloom involved these days, there’s an authenticity to the current talk of Hearts winning major honours, perhaps even the title one day.

As their supporters prepare to march on Hampden again tomorrow to face Hibs, the part of all of those who stood on the right side of history won’t be forgotten.

A new venue with just over 70,000 seats called Generali Stadium, the cost of which is estimated at 1.2 billion euros. On this occasion, all the Nerazzurri and Rossoneri leaders were out to discuss the future of the two enemy brothers of Italian football. Despite everything, the Rossoneri decided to go big during the last summer transfer window by spending €164 million to strengthen themselves, in particular, with three very expensive recruits: Spanish defender Mario Gila (€30 million), former Belgian left winger from Strasbourg Diego Moreira (€50 million) and Portuguese striker Gonçalo Ramos (€74 million). The former PSG striker even became the most expensive recruit in the club’s history.

But for the moment, the team coached by Ruben Amorim is struggling to respond. Fifth last season, AC Milan are still in fifth place in the standings this year, seven points behind the domestic leader. Nothing to call into question the future of the Portuguese coach according to Gerry Cardinale. The latter even took advantage of this media tour to announce that Milan still planned to recruit. “We are in the process of rebuilding the team and, although I appreciate the new arrivals, the ones who stayed and the players I parted ways with, it will probably take two more transfer windows to finalize everything. A rumor that was quickly nipped in the bud by the Gones.

#1539. Spalletti open to 3-4-2-1 at Genoa but expects few changes with Napoli next

Luciano Spalletti is ready to shift from a 3-5-2 to a 3-4-2-1 at Genoa, with Alajbegovic among the options behind the striker. With eight players injured and Napoli due on Sunday, he expects his team to stay broadly the same.

Luciano Spalletti is ready to tweak his shape at Genoa without tearing up his team. On the eve of the trip, the Juventus coach said one very small positional change turns the 3-5-2 into a 3-4-2-1. Anyone, he added, can fill the two roles behind the striker.

He named Alajbegovic, Boga and Zhegrova as options in that zone. Kolo Muani was his example of the profile he has in mind. Spalletti said the forward can play partly as a number 10 and partly as a wide forward. Sarr has recovered and is available.

Tuttosport expects Alajbegovic to possibly replace Kolo Muani behind Woltemade, and sees Cambiaso as the only left-flank option with Celik injured.

The fixture list explains the caution. The trip to Genoa is the first of two games in five days. Spalletti is weighing a few rotations partly because of the second of those games, Sky Sport reported. Asked about Napoli, the coach said everything has to be taken into account. He still expects the team to stay broadly the same.

Spalletti also said his players are fully focused and have the right mentality. That follows a mixed run. Juventus lost at home to Lazio on 18 October. Afterwards Spalletti said his side had shown fragility that starts in the mind. He added that tactical systems change nothing without hunger, passion, courage and character. A draw with Rennes followed.

The win at Lecce began to make up for both results. McKennie volleyed in a Douglas Luiz free kick in the 29th minute. Douglas Luiz added the second four minutes before half-time.

Spalletti described Genoa as an extremely hard opponent, citing both the atmosphere at their ground and their tactics. He warned they can use their physical strength at set pieces and also run in behind defences. Above all, he said, the side carries Daniele De Rossi’s fighting spirit.

The warning on dead balls fits recent meetings between the clubs. Six of the last ten goals between the clubs came from set pieces: two from corners, one from a throw-in and three from penalties.

🗣️ "We must put in convincing performances"

Luciano Spalletti looks ahead to #GenoaJuve in his pre-match press conference ⤵️

🗞️ https://t.co/r2x4ICLz15 pic.twitter.com/tWcJLMx0Ia

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 27, 2026

History still favours Juventus. They have lost only one of their last 12 Serie A games against Genoa, with nine wins and two draws. They have also won the last four. That lone defeat was 2-1 at the Ferraris on 6 May 2022. Juventus have scored 233 goals against Genoa, more than any other club in the league.

After Genoa, Juventus host Massimiliano Allegri’s Napoli in Serie A Matchday 10 on Sunday 1 November, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1537. Cup semi-final triumph over rivals Hearts would be the ideal moment to pick up first win as Hibs boss, admits Marink Reedijk

By ANTHONY BROWN, PRESS ASSOCIATION SPORT

Published: 14:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 14:01 EDT, 30 October 2026

Marink Reedijk is relishing a “special match” as he aims to belatedly ignite his Hibernian reign with victory over high-flying city rivals Hearts in Sunday’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final.

After three defeats and a draw in his first four matches in charge of the Hibs, the Dutchman goes into his first Edinburgh derby eyeing a first win since succeeding David Gray in September.

Hearts, third in the Premiership, have won all four previous meetings between the two Capital clubs at Hampden, including the 2012 Scottish Cup final, and Reedijk has been made well aware of the importance of the derby during his five weeks in Edinburgh.

“It’s a special match in several ways,” said Reedijk, who revealed that experienced striker Martin Boyle will return after illness.

“This is the type of match you look forward to because it’s not only the derby, it’s also a semi-final, and it’s one step away from a final, so that is a double way of excitement.

“You don’t need to ask anyone here about the derby because they will tell you, and this is also the beautiful thing about it. And we have someone in our staff (former Hibs player Guillaume Beuzelin) who experienced a few, and therefore, of course, he told us about it and he prepared us for what we can expect.”

Marink Reedijk is hoping to pick up his first win as Hibernian boss in the Premier Sports Cup

Hibs celebrate opening the scoring at St Mirren in midweek but had to settle for a 1-1 draw

After the joy of leading Beveren to an unbeaten title triumph in the Belgian second tier last season, Reedijk has found himself struggling for results during a testing start to his Hibs tenure.

“It is interesting because everybody recognises last year with Beveren, but in the beginning at Beveren, we had the same sort of spells,” he said.

“The only thing which is different is that I had a start where we had a pre-season, and you could already put some things in place (in friendlies), and here I started immediately with competitive matches.

“But I have been in these situations as well with Beveren, and we focused on the things we did, and trusted the way we did it, and focused on not only the results.

“I know the results are important, but if the result is not there, is the performance there? And if the performance is there, then it’s a matter of time.

“The performances are getting better and better and better, and therefore, like in Beveren, I think if you keep on progressing, the results will come.”

Reedijk will come up against one of his Beveren ‘Invincibles’ from last season in goalkeeper Beau Reus, who joined Hearts in the summer.

“It’s a special connection,” said the Hibs boss. “We will always be linked – not only him and me, but the whole team. Together for the rest of our lives, because of the performance of last year.

“However, since Wednesday evening, I don’t feel this at the moment. It will be after Sunday night that this feeling comes back again, because I want to win the match. He is someone who will always be part of my journey.”

#1536. £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Some surprised faces then when Moyes said later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”

The game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes said that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”

In the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

De Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender said: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and showed that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l

"Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young says that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev

Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh

Dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

There will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6

Tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

Spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a big chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

De Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

Johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

That opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

That was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

"What a chance this was!"Brennan Johnson had the chance to put Everton in front against his former club 😯 pic.twitter.com/fUi7t6hX7t

Everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

What is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

Antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors currently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

George does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

Spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

We are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

An uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

There will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

There has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

That is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

Tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

Gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Big question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

Spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

"Solanke is a crucial player"Roberto De Zerbi on the importance of Dominic Solanke being fit for Spurs 💪 pic.twitter.com/FNWNsTWdt8

Coventry City vs Brighton & Hove Albion (14:00)

Manchester United vs Manchester City (16:30)

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

🎧🫡 Thierno Barry ahead of today's clash in North London. pic.twitter.com/mwlsKH8Pid

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van de Ven, Van Hecke, Robertson; Tonali, Bentancur, Fernandes; Savio, Solankem, Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

After scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @SpursOfficial. COYB! ✊#TOTEVE pic.twitter.com/mOcCayRUfm

Roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1534. Spalletti apologises after Genoa defeat leaves Juventus level with Napoli on 14 points

Juventus lost 2-0 at Genoa on Serie A Matchday 9, a third league defeat in nine games that undid the good work of the win at Lecce. Napoli, the next visitors to Turin, now have the same points total.

The defeat came on 28 October 2026, with both Genoa goals arriving before half-time. Luciano Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. The result came three days after a 2-0 win at Lecce on Matchday 8. That win, built on first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz, now looks like a false dawn.

Genoa needed little time to break through, and Ehizibue was the man to do it. His goal ended a 504-minute run without a Genoa goal against Juventus in Serie A, going back to an Albert Gudmundsson strike on 15 December 2023, Sportmediaset reported.

Baldanzi then exposed the Juventus defence again. Scoring and setting up a goal in one Serie A match was new for Baldanzi.

Juventus’s best chance of the first half came just before the interval. Kalulu shot off target after a pass from McKennie. Spalletti sent on Edon Zhegrova and Nick Woltemade for the second half. The changes did not help, and Genoa held firm. The win moved Daniele De Rossi’s side up to 10 points.

The coach did not hide from the performance. His team were beaten in every area of the pitch and must improve physically and in their fighting spirit, Spalletti told the club’s website. In his press conference he pointed to a lack of physical impact and to lost duels.

He also noted that the level shown at Lecce had not been repeated. There had been no training session between the two matches. That short turnaround is part of his explanation.

The evening got worse elsewhere. Napoli won 4-1 at Monza, with goals from Højlund, Politano, Rafa Marín and De Bruyne. Their coach, Massimiliano Allegri, watched from the stands. He was serving a two-match ban picked up against Roma.

Spalletti described Napoli as a very strong team. Both sides sit well behind the top of the table, so the meeting carries weight for each.

The response he wants will have to come quickly, with little time to work on the training ground. A home crowd that received an apology on Wednesday will be watching closely.

#1532. Under-fire Dons boss Stephen Robinson isn't seeking any assurances from club chiefs over his job

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 13:48 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 14:02 EDT, 30 October 2026

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson insists he has not sought any assurances over his position from chairman Dave Cormack despite a woeful run of form.

A 1-0 home defeat to Falkirk on Wednesday night left the Dons slumped in ninth position in the Premiership table with just one win in their last five matches.

A section of the Pittodrie crowd turned on Robinson and his players and booed them off the pitch after another insipid display.

Heading into today’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final clash with Rangers at Hampden, there have been some suggestions that Robinson’s position could be under serious threat.

Whilst accepting the criticism from fans, the under-fire boss insisted it has been business as usual in terms of his conversations with Cormack and new chief executive Adrian Bevington.

‘No, I’m not seeking any assurances,’ said Robinson. ‘I have just had my normal conversations.

Under-fire Dons boss Robinson is not seeking assurances from club hierarchy over his job

‘I speak to the chairman once a week and I speak to Adrian once a week. That’s no different than any other week.

‘So, no, there’s been nothing different. We know the results over the last couple of weeks haven’t been good enough.

‘No one is getting away from that fact and ultimately we deserve the criticism we got. I deserve the criticism, I don’t hide behind that. And I don’t try to throw players under the bus.

‘The players know it needs to be better and they are all in that together. There are no factions, there are no people going off on their own, everyone wants to turn that around.

‘I know given time, this can be very successful. But I also live in the real world. You need to get results that give yourself longevity.

‘Certainly, everybody wants time, but you don’t get given time in football. We’re all well aware of that and results are what dictates that. And what a place to start at Hampden.’

Ahead of this evening’s clash at Hampden, Robinson believes it will be the perfect opportunity for Aberdeen to turn their season around if they can beat Rangers.

Robinson was typically animated during a match that saw his team lose 1-0 to Falkirk

He also claimed that all of the pressure will be on Rangers, given the expectation on them to beat an Aberdeen side who have toiled for much of the season.

‘You haven’t got time to feel sorry for yourself, if there is a moment to put it right a semi final at Hampden is that time,’ he added.

‘As a footballer you always get another chance, sometimes as a manager you don’t and what a chance it is to go to Hampden, a full house with a big support with us. It is certainly the right place to do it and we believe we can.

‘Every semi-final that I’ve been in with Motherwell and St Mirren, we were not expected to win. So I know how to motivate teams and the staff know how to get teams to believe.

‘It’s certainly an opportunity. All the pressure will be on Rangers, and the expectation will be on Rangers.’

Earlier this week, Rangers boss Derek McInnes, who spent eight years with the Dons, backed Robinson to succeed at Pittodrie if he is given time to turn it around.

‘Until you are in this position, you don’t realise how difficult things are and the parameters you have to work under, Derek obviously does,’ added Robinson.

‘I have nothing but total respect for him. He is one of the top managers in the country. Everybody wants time but you don’t get given time in football, we are all well aware of that and results are what dictates that.

‘We face a really good Rangers side. Derek’s built a really good squad, a really big, athletic, strong squad. We are coming up against a team that are in form, a team that are winning football matches.

‘We know that we have to be better than what we are. I’ve been to semi-finals before and I’ve always been the underdog. No doubt that would be exactly the same, rightly. It’s up to us to turn that around.’

Robinson's under-performing Dons team are languishing ninth in Premiership table

On team news, Robinson added: ‘We’ve got a problem at the back, of course, that’s been well documented, with Lewis Mayo, Mats Knoester and Dan Happe. Dan is suspended, but he’s actually ill as well, so he’s got the virus.

‘Kristers Tobers has had a little bit of a setback. There’s a little bit of swelling on his knee, so he won’t be available for selection tomorrow. Chris Cadden won’t be available tomorrow either.

‘We haven’t had to seek our troubles, but again, as I always say, somebody’s misfortune is somebody else’s opportunity.

‘It’s a chance for people who maybe haven’t had opportunities, or people who haven’t been fit, to stand up and be counted. As I said, there’s no better stage than Hampden to do that.

‘It’s a mild hamstring injury (Cadden’s injury). We’re hoping he could be fit for the Hibs game, but at this early stage, it’s still very hard to say. We just know he won’t be available with the quick turnaround for Saturday.’

#1529. Guys like Makhanya and Sterling should feel welcome to speak the truth more often if Rangers are to finally throw off their serial losers tag

Published: 14:15 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:19 EDT, 30 October 2026

Olwethu Makhanya is shaping up to be everything Rangers needed in their search for defensive reinforcements in the summer.

A solid presence at the back, a young and hungry talent very much on the up and a leader with real personality.

If it didn’t look so likely that someone will come in before long and offer the Ibrox board the chance to make a healthy profit on the £3million they paid to Philadelphia Union for the 22-year-old, you’d put him down as a nailed-on future captain.

He’s helping set the standards required if Rangers are to overhaul arch-rivals Celtic in the title race and was absolutely spot-on after rescuing an ill-deserved point with a late equaliser at Tynecastle on Wednesday when bemoaning a lack of character at the start of the second half and the fact Hearts worked harder and showed more desire.

It’s the kind of honesty many Ibrox sides of recent years have needed. A public kick up the backside for underperforming team-mates, the footballing equivalent of getting the whip out and a necessary form of assurance for frustrated supporters that there is at least someone inside the dressing room who feels the way they feel, who wants what they want.

It’s why it is to be hoped that manager Derek McInnes’ remarks the morning after were not some attempt to gently slap down the South African.

Defender Olwethu Makhanya questioned the character of this Rangers squad midweek

McInnes, of course, is entitled to his own opinion about the reserves of character within his squad. Maybe he did disagree with Makhanya’s version of events, or his questioning of the side’s resilience.

Alternative viewpoints delivered respectfully are fine. More than fine. They are a sign of a healthy workplace.

It just felt like it was all skirting a little too close to a chastisement of the big centre-back’s comments.

And whether that was the intention or not, being seen to chastise a player whose sentiments are clearly coming from the right place, from a burning desire to make a club with one league crown in 15 years be successful again, is not necessarily the right course of action to take.

It happened, if you remember, with Dujon Sterling back in Philippe Clement’s first season as boss when an April collapse that involved a home draw with Celtic, a 3-2 loss at Ross County and a stalemate at Dundee pretty much killed off hopes of lifting the title.

‘We owe ourselves a performance… because we have been s**t the past three games,’ said Sterling in the aftermath at Dens Park. ‘We are fighting for a title and the way we are playing, it is as if we are not playing for anything. It’s like the season is dead and it is a dead-rubber game.’

It felt like a cry from the heart, a desperate plea to those around him to breathe life into a dying campaign. It was a truth that had to be told.

Clement, meanwhile, was already well on the way to losing the plot at that point, claiming his side were ‘moral winners’ after snatching that draw with Celtic thanks to a late goal and insisting that he was happy his side ‘bossed it’ at Dens.

Criticising Sterling afterwards just made him look even more like he didn’t get it, had lost all sight of what being at Rangers — or any club that has to win at all costs — was about.

‘It’s the words of a player who is disappointed because we lost points and maybe lacks a bit of experience in that way,’ stated the Belgian waffler. ‘That’s things for young players to learn and become better in. It’s more talking out of frustration.’

Manager Derek McInnes disagreed with Makhanya's comments following the Hearts game

That’s the standard response from football persons, of course. The whole business, for some time, has revolved around young players having it battered into them that it’s better to say nothing, to drone on dead-eyed through interviews, bat everything away, put their personality on the bonfire, ‘don’t get too up or too down’.

It’s nonsense, though. McInnes honed his trade in a Nine-In-A-Row Rangers dressing room full of huge characters who built unbreakable bonds while still being able to dig each other out, demand more, be confrontational.

Sure, it happened more behind doors than in the public gaze, but things are different now from the way they were 30 years ago. Social media has changed the landscape so drastically. Fan narratives do drive boardroom decisions and that has arguably been clearer at Ibrox in recent times than anywhere.

There’s a concern still living just under the surface among a large number of Rangers fans that there is an ingrained loser mentality at their club and plenty of evidence to back that up.

Admittedly, the playing staff has changed drastically since then, but it is impossible to forget Billy Dodds reflecting on his time as a first-team coach for interim boss Barry Ferguson and talking about how 70 per cent of signings had been wrong and that the dressing room had a number of weak characters who couldn’t handle adversity.

Even before Danny Rohl left for Red Bull Salzburg last season, he talked about players being ‘too lazy to recover’ in key moments. He also spoke about how some of the squad were ‘very quiet’ when he first took over.

Supporters of Rangers, treated to some amount of failure and in-house claptrap over the last decade or more, need to see evidence that those on the field care the way they do.

The kind of frank analysis delivered by Makhanya — in a calm and considered way, it should be said — need not be the negative so many inside football are programmed to think.

If anything, seeing guys wear their hearts on their sleeve can serve to strengthen the relationship between fans and their favourites in difficult times.

The modern-day audience have had enough of failing players promising to learn lessons and move on. At outfits judged on league titles and facing pressure to win every week, learning lessons is the last thing on the agenda. You really ought to know what needs done by that stage.

Rangers have drawn two of their last three and currently trail leaders Celtic by four points

Punters want to see the real people behind the branding, measure their minerals. And we’re on about more than just those cringeworthy features on club TV where players quiz each other on whether they prefer Jaffa Cakes or KitKats while playing a game of ping-pong. It’s showing a bit of what’s really inside, being properly authentic, that resonates.

In fairness to McInnes, his messaging as Rangers boss has generally been good so far. He didn’t shy away from the paucity of those performances in losing in Europe to Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec.

He hasn’t indulged in deflection. He confronted the speculation that was already beginning to swirl about his future after that Jablonec catastrophe, handled it well and steered the side to safer ground with two excellent back-to-back wins against Celtic.

He has been honest and upfront and entirely understanding of the expectations that rest upon his shoulders.

His team is still guilty of switching off in games. Centre-back Manny Fernandez, although the manager must back him publicly, is the epitome of that.

His players still have to show they can be consistent enough to prevail against a Celtic side that is most definitely there for the taking. They need to keep the pedal to the metal and to deliver 90-minute performances or, at least, maintain control throughout.

It is a squad light on trophies on the CV and with a number of younger players. It is going to need regular reminders as this race plays out.

If Makhanya or Sterling or anyone else want to take it upon themselves to put those reminders out there, it shouldn’t be regarded as a bad thing. And it definitely shouldn’t be discouraged.

#1528. Carnevali calls Juventus situation ‘not acceptable’ as squad enters retreat before Napoli

Juventus will stay together in a training retreat at the JTC Continassa from Friday 30 October until Sunday's game against Napoli, after a blunt meeting between Giovanni Carnevali, the players and Luciano Spalletti. That home fixture is now widely seen as decisive for the coach's future and the direction of the season.

A direct meeting with chief executive Giovanni Carnevali has put the Juventus players and their coach under heavy pressure before Napoli’s visit.

The trigger was the loss in Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck in the 12th minute, and Tommaso Baldanzi added a second in the 28th. Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. He said his side had been beaten in every area. He added that they had to raise their physical level and fighting spirit.

The squad travelled back by train overnight. The players went to the Continassa the next morning. Management spoke to them there before training. Carnevali reminded them of their responsibilities to the owners, the club and the fans. He said the coaching staff still had the club’s trust, Adnkronos reported. He also asked for a strong and concrete reaction on the pitch. With the club’s agreement, Spalletti then chose to keep the players together at the training centre until kick-off.

Clubs rarely call this kind of retreat. It shows how serious the mood is at the Continassa. The message from the top is twofold. Public backing for the coaching staff comes paired with pressure for results. That places heavy weight on a single fixture.

Both sides have four wins, two draws and three defeats from nine games, Corriere dello Sport reported. Napoli sit seventh and Juventus eighth.

The gap lies in front of goal. Napoli have scored 17 times. Juventus have managed 11. Juventus have conceded only 10, however. Those figures are consistent with a side whose problems lie more in attack than in defence. A reaction against Napoli would need goals as well as fighting spirit.

Napoli will be without their coach. Massimiliano Allegri’s two-match ban covers their league games against Monza and Juventus. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea also fined him 10,000 euros. The sanction followed his abuse of match officials and later behaviour in the changing rooms during Napoli’s 3-3 draw with Roma. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri later said he had decided to drop it. That leaves Juventus facing a Napoli side without Allegri in charge at a moment when their own coach is under pressure.

The last meeting between the sides in Turin, on 25 January 2026, ended in a 3-0 Juventus win at the Allianz Stadium.

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1527. Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”

What an important week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães said. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”

These are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”

Raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

Mikel Arteta launched a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

“In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” said Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

“I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

“You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

“I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. We had really good periods but didn’t score and after that they can suffocate you especially when they decided to be really physical and very direct and we had to overcome a situation that in my opinion was absolutely unacceptable at this level. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

“Are you surprised? Are you surprised? No. OK.

“Ezri does nothing. Just watch it. We have a lot of cameras and VAR, and we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing,” he added.

“I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”

Guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

I’m so upset – it’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of a season, of the championship. I’ve seen it 10 times, to make sure, because I saw it live and said ‘It’s not possible at this level it can be a penalty’. Because it’s a judo roll, that’s what it is. It cannot happen.

I’ve been in football for 27 or 28 years - it’s not a penalty in any game, in any league, in any context.

Sunderland are a really, really good team and I don’t want to take any credit away from them. It’s been extremely tough and I’m really happy that we’ve done it.

Reinildo is booked for a foul on Saka. The home fans are getting annoyed with what they perceive as diving from some of the Arsenal attackers: “Same old Arsenal, always cheating” is the chant of choice just now. Odegaard also went down a moment ago after a foul from Angulo.

Gabriel strides forward from defence and sweeps a left-foot shot from 25 yards. It’s a good effort that fades just wide of the far post with Roefs scrambling across his line.

Sunderland will be really pleased with the first quarter. They’re defending solidly and look a threat on the break, thanks in part to some outstanding hold-up play from Brian Brobbey. Saka’s volley is the only shot on target at either end.

The pattern of the game has been established, with Arsenal dominating the ball and Sunderland picking their moments to press and then counter-attack.

Sunderland break promisingly down the right. Mukiele drives an angled low cross that only just evades Angulo at the far post.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

Enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

Arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

We’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

We know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

When will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the new £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Saturday night Gunners ❤️‍🔥🤝 Presented by @deel

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

#1526. French team: injuries will shake up Zinédine Zidane’s list

Learning the job of coach also begins there for Zinédine Zidane. As in September when he had to deal with the absences of William Saliba, Aurélien Tchouameni, then a little later of Ibrahima Konaté (replaced by Leny Yoro), the former playmaker should be faced with a new headache when putting together his new list, which he will unveil this Friday. In central defense, still no William Saliba, unavailable for several more weeks, nor Maxence Lacroix, victim of a torn hamstring and perhaps absent until the end of the year.

Three places seem reserved for Dayot Upamecano, Jérémy Jacquet and Ibrahima Konaté. For the last folding seat, we can therefore imagine a fight between Leny Yoro, less efficient with Manchester United but interesting last month with the Blues, Lucas Hernandez, convincing in his last outings with PSG, or why not Wesley Fofana, author of a good performance against Manchester United this weekend. On the right, Jules Koundé remains uncertain after missing Barça’s shocks against Real Madrid and PSG due to a sprained ankle. We could therefore see Pierre Kalulu again in this position. For second place, it’s not easy to establish a hierarchy. Malo Gusto does not play at Chelsea, Jonathan Clauss (34) lives again in Nice but does not really meet the criteria of Zinédine Zidane, keen to prepare for the future. As for Benjamin Pavard, he is injured. Andy Diouf could occupy this position but Zidane insisted on his wish to see him on the left during the first meeting.

What about the midfielder? Manu Koné should not be recovered after his thigh injury but Zinédine Zidane will be able to count on the returns of Aurélien Tchouameni, Warren Zaire-Emery and Adrien Rabiot, scorer with AC Milan on Saturday in the derby against Inter (3-1). It is very likely that Eduardo Camavinga and Lucas Da Cunha will be renewed. Rayan Cherki was also included in the midfielders last month, leaving little room for surprises in this sector.

We know that the coach is not left out in offensive positions, but he could still play a few unexpected cards after calling up Estéban Lepaul last month. Ousmane Dembélé is out, Michael Olise is doubtful after being injured against Dortmund on Saturday, and Estéban Lepaul is injured in the left ankle. A situation favorable to Marcus Thuram, in form with Inter Milan? This is a possibility according to Téléfoot. The highly anticipated Éli-Junior Kroupi could still wait after several months of absence. The Bournemouth striker was still a decisive passer in 22 minutes this weekend against Leeds.

#1525. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.
